title: U.S. government equity stake, CHIPS Act funding and SoftBank/Arm agreements
summary: This community centers on the U.S. government's equity stake in Intel, tied to CHIPS Act funding and the Department of Commerce agreements, with Intel's risk factors on pausing Intel 14A and depending on third-party foundries linked to it [0000050863-25-000179:0068][0000050863-25-000109:0063]. The U.S. Government Agreement with the DOC accelerated $5.7 billion of Direct Funding Agreement disbursements and $3.2 billion under Secure Enclave, in exchange for common stock, escrowed shares and warrants [0000050863-26-000011:0127]. NVIDIA's filings contribute the 2020 Share Purchase Agreement among NVIDIA, NVIDIA Holdings, Arm, SoftBank and Vision Fund, which appears in its exhibit index [0001045810-25-000023:0131].
findings: The transactions eliminate contractual rights to receive future grant funds under the commercial CHIPS Act agreement and may limit the company's ability to secure government grants in the future [0000050863-25-000179:0068].

The U.S. government was one of the company's largest stockholders at 5.8% as of September 27, 2025, and may acquire up to an additional 3.2% as Secure Enclave disbursements are received [0000050863-25-000179:0068].

Intel's filing says that pausing Intel 14A could cause significant impairments on foundry assets, with over $100 billion of property, plant and equipment, net, and could forfeit incentives under the $7.9 billion Direct Funding Agreement [0000050863-25-000109:0063].

The warrants to purchase up to 241 million shares at $20.00 become exercisable if the company were to cease to directly or indirectly own at least 51% of its foundry business [0000050863-26-000011:0127].

The private placement sold 87 million shares of common stock to SoftBank Group at $23.00 per share, for an aggregate cash purchase price of $2.0 billion, completed September 26, 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0127].
The company has no long-term contract with TSMC, and only TSMC and Samsung are named as foundries capable of producing the leading-edge nodes its products need [0000050863-25-000109:0063].

title: Intel's Altera sale to Silver Lake and NAND divestiture to SK hynix
summary: The Altera transaction is governed by a transaction agreement, a separation agreement with SLP, and later amendments, with Intel retaining a 49% minority stake [0000050863-25-000074:0022][0000050863-25-000179:0072]. The NAND sale closed in two phases, and a final release and settlement agreement with SK hynix addressed penalties under their manufacturing and sale agreement [0000050863-25-000074:0021][0000050863-25-000109:0026].
findings: On April 14, 2025, Intel signed a transaction agreement with SLP VII Gryphon Aggregator, an affiliate of Silver Lake Partners, to sell 51% of Altera, a wholly owned subsidiary [0000050863-25-000109:0026].

The Altera sale is expected to yield about $4.4 billion in net cash proceeds, and $1.0 billion of the purchase price is deferred into two $500 million installments due by December 31, 2026 and December 31, 2027 [0000050863-25-000074:0022].
Intel agreed to fund Altera separation costs and expenses up to $277 million under a separation agreement with SLP [0000050863-25-000074:0022].

Amendment No. 1 to the Transaction Agreement is dated August 11, 2025, and an Amended and Restated Transaction Agreement is dated September 12, 2025, both among Intel, Intel Americas, Altera and SLP VII Gryphon Aggregator [0000050863-25-000179:0072].

Upon closing, Intel expects to deconsolidate Altera as a variable interest entity and apply the equity method to its retained minority investment, and Altera's assets held for sale totaled $2,310 million as of June 28, 2025 [0000050863-25-000109:0026].

Intel sold its NAND memory technology and manufacturing business, the NAND OpCo Business, to SK hynix; the first phase closed in December 2021 and the second phase closed March 27, 2025, with $1.9 billion of proceeds recorded [0000050863-25-000074:0021].

In connection with the second NAND closing, Intel entered into a final release and settlement agreement with SK hynix tied to penalties under their manufacturing and sale agreement, recognizing a net charge of $94 million [0000050863-25-000109:0026].

Intel amended its 364-day credit facility from $8.0 billion to $5.0 billion and extended its maturity to January 2026, and it had $1.5 billion of commercial paper outstanding as of March 29, 2025 [0000050863-25-000074:0022].

title: Intel CCG, DCAI and NEX segments and competition
summary: This community centers on Intel's Client Computing Group (CCG), Data Center and AI (DCAI) and Networking and Edge (NEX) segments, which together form Intel Products and are designed by Intel and manufactured by Intel Foundry and third-party suppliers [0000050863-26-000011:0010]. The passages show that SoC products span CCG, DCAI and NEX, and that the DCAI and NEX businesses target 5G base stations and network infrastructure [0000050863-25-000074:0035]. The competitive picture is mainly about Intel against AMD, Apple and MediaTek in client processors [0000050863-26-000011:0010].
findings: CCG's primary competitor is AMD, which like Intel designs processors based on the x86 architecture, while ARM-based rivals include Apple with its M series and MediaTek with its Kompanio products [0000050863-26-000011:0010].
Intel states it operates in a highly competitive market and expects this environment to further intensify in 2026 [0000050863-26-000011:0010].

In fiscal 2024, CCG generated $30,290 million of revenue and $10,920 million of operating income, versus $12,817 million of revenue and $1,338 million of operating income for DCAI and $5,842 million of revenue and $931 million of operating income for NEX [0000050863-25-000009:0111].

In fiscal 2024, Intel Foundry reported $17,543 million of revenue and an operating loss of $13,408 million, which sits alongside the Intel Products segments that rely on it for manufacturing [0000050863-25-000009:0111].

In Q1 2024, notebook revenue was $4.7 billion, up $1.3 billion from Q1 2023, and desktop revenue was $2.5 billion, up $582 million, with notebook and desktop volumes rising 39% and 29% respectively [0000050863-24-000076:0034].
Intel's Smart Capital approach includes continued use of external foundries alongside capacity investments and government incentives [0000050863-24-000124:0037].
The 2025 Restructuring Plan reallocated resources toward Intel's core client and server businesses by reducing investment in lower-priority programs [0000050863-25-000109:0040].
Intel describes its Intel Core Ultra processors as designed to enable advanced AI capabilities, and says AI integration will remain a key differentiator for CCG [0000050863-26-000011:0010].

title: Intel edge networking, Xeon and FlexRAN products, and climate regulation risk
summary: Intel's filings link its On-Premises Edge, Enterprise Networking and Telecommunication Networks platforms to Xeon processors, FlexCore and FlexRAN software [0000050863-25-000009:0025]. The community also covers Intel's networking and data center products, including Ethernet controllers, network adapters and IPUs, which the filing says complement its Xeon processors [0000050863-26-000011:0017]. Its risk factors add environmental and climate regulation, including California's climate disclosure requirements and the EU's Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive [0000050863-25-000009:0077].
findings: Intel says it leads 5G core network deployments and that its customers are tier-one global communication service providers and their equipment suppliers [0000050863-25-000009:0025] [0000050863-25-000009:0026].
Intel says the IPUs are manufactured at an external foundry, on process nodes that vary by product [0000050863-26-000011:0017].

Intel announced Crescent Island, a GPU on the Xe3P architecture aimed at AI inference in data centers, and says it is also developing Jaguar Shores as its next-generation GPU architecture [0000050863-26-000011:0016].
The 5th Gen Intel Xeon Scalable processors, introduced in late 2023, use the same platform as the 4th Gen with faster DDR5 memory and a larger last-level cache [0000050863-26-000011:0016].
Intel warns that its corporate responsibility initiatives could expose it to heightened scrutiny and financial, legal and reputational risks [0000050863-25-000009:0077].

Intel says environmental and health regulations on PFAS could limit semiconductor manufacturing, and that PFAS has limited technically and commercially feasible alternatives [0000050863-26-000011:0087].

title: Intel SCIP partnerships with Brookfield, Apollo and Bain Capital
summary: This community centers on Intel's Semiconductor Co-Investment Program (SCIP), under which outside investors supply capital for Intel's fabs while Intel keeps operating them [0000050863-24-000124:0016]. The Arizona SCIP was tied to a 2022 joint investment with Brookfield, and the Ireland SCIP involved Apollo's 2024 purchase of a 49% interest tied to Fab 34 [0000050863-24-000124:0017] [0000050863-25-000009:0015]. The filings also link these deals to the IMS minority stake sales to Bain Capital, the CHIPS Act funding, and risk factors about penalties and financing that name Intel [0000050863-24-000124:0017] [0000050863-26-000011:0068].
findings: Apollo closed a transaction in the second quarter of 2024 involving the sale of 49% of Intel's interest in Ireland SCIP for net proceeds of $11.0 billion, and Ireland SCIP has the rights to operate Fab 34 in Leixlip, Ireland [0000050863-24-000124:0016].

Intel has an unrecognized commitment to fund its share of Arizona SCIP construction costs of $29.0 billion, and its remaining unfunded contribution under the Brookfield definitive agreement was $10.5 billion as of December 28, 2024 [0000050863-24-000124:0017] [0000050863-25-000009:0154].
Intel recognized a $755 million charge in the fourth quarter of 2024 for penalties it expects to pay in connection with Ireland SCIP construction delays [0000050863-26-000011:0068].

A pause or discontinuation of Intel 14A could accelerate Intel's move to third-party foundry services and could require substantial additional payments to its SCIP partners [0000050863-26-000011:0066].

Intel closed agreements to sell a combined 32% minority stake in its IMS business, including a 20% stake to Bain Capital and a 10% stake to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, with net proceeds of $1.4 billion [0000050863-24-000124:0017].

Intel signed an agreement with the US Department of Commerce for up to $7.9 billion in direct funding under the commercial CHIPS Act program and may receive up to $3 billion under the Secure Enclave program, and it expects to benefit from the Advanced Manufacturing Investment Credit [0000050863-25-000009:0015].
Intel expects greater than $25 billion of capital offsets through its SCIP partnerships with Brookfield and Apollo [0000050863-25-000009:0015].

Mobileye is a consolidated business in which Intel holds a noncontrolling interest of 12%, and Intel sold Class A shares in a 2023 secondary offering for net proceeds of $1.6 billion [0000050863-24-000124:0017].

title: Intel Section 13(r) Russia sanctions disclosure and executive ties
summary: This community centers on Intel's Section 13(r) disclosure of dealings with two Russian parties subject to U.S. sanctions: the Federal Security Service of the Russian Federation and Positive Technologies [0000050863-25-000179:0071]. The disclosure states that the FSB dealings are explicitly authorized by General License 1B and the Positive Technologies communications resumed under an OFAC license, with no gross revenues or net profits directly associated with either [0000050863-25-000179:0071]. Yeary and Christoph Schell, who are tied to Mobileye Global Inc., and all of the passages are from Intel's filings rather than NVIDIA's or AMD's [0000050863-25-000009:0087][0000050863-25-000009:0086].
findings: Intel has suspended sales in Russia, but there may be a need to file documents or engage with the FSB as Intel winds up its local Russian offices [0000050863-25-000179:0071].
Intel had coordinated disclosure of security vulnerabilities with the firm and resumed those communications under an OFAC license [0000050863-25-000179:0071].
Section 13(r) requires disclosure of sanctioned dealings even when they are conducted in compliance with applicable law [0000050863-25-000179:0071].

The same Section 13(r) disclosure about the FSB and Positive Technologies appears in Intel filings for the quarter ended March 30, 2024 [0000050863-24-000076:0047] and again for the quarter ended September 27, 2025 [0000050863-25-000179:0071].

Yeary has been Interim Executive Chair of Intel's Board since December 2024 and also serves on the board of Mobileye Global Inc., which the filing describes as Intel's subsidiary and an autonomous driving technology company [0000050863-25-000009:0087].

Christoph Schell has been Intel's Executive Vice President and Chief Commercial Officer since March 2022 and is a member of the Board of Directors of Mobileye Global, Inc. [0000050863-25-000009:0086].
David Zinsner has been Interim Co-Chief Executive Officer of Intel since December 2024 and Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer since January 2022 [0000050863-25-000009:0087].
April Miller Boise has been Intel's Executive Vice President and Chief Legal Officer since July 2022, leading its global legal, trade, and government affairs team [0000050863-25-000009:0086].

title: Intel bonds, revolving credit facilities and IDM 2.0 government incentives
summary: The bonds are unsecured general obligations issued under loan agreements with those two bodies [0000050863-25-000009:0138].
findings: Intel remarketed $438 million of Chandler bonds in the second quarter of 2024, carrying a 4.00% coupon and maturing in 2049, with optional tender starting in February 2029 [0000050863-24-000124:0023].

In 2024 Intel expanded its 5-year revolving facility from $5.0 billion to $7.0 billion and its 364-day facility from $5.0 billion to $8.0 billion, extending their maturities to February 2029 and January 2025 [0000050863-24-000124:0023].
In January 2025 Intel amended the 364-day facility from $8.0 billion down to $5.0 billion and extended its maturity to January 2026 [0000050863-25-000009:0138].

Intel expected to replace or amend the $5.0 billion 364-day facility before its January 2026 maturity, and had no borrowings outstanding under its revolving facilities as of December 27, 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0155].
As of December 28, 2024, Intel's Oregon and Arizona bonds totaled $423 million at 3.80% to 4.10% due 2035 to 2040, plus $438 million at 4.00% due June 2049 [0000050863-25-000009:0137].

Intel said that incentives below its expectations would increase its anticipated cash requirements and/or potentially curtail planned investments, while incentives above expectations would let it increase the pace and size of its IDM 2.0 investments [0000050863-24-000124:0051].

title: U.S. government equity stake and CHIPS Act grant risks
summary: This community centers on risk factors from the U.S. government becoming a significant stockholder through equity issuances and an amendment to the commercial CHIPS Act agreement in the third quarter of 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0069]. The filing refers to net income attributable to Intel, and it ties these transactions to the company's broader reliance on government grants and alternative financing [0000050863-26-000011:0068]. sales exposure, demand and margin variation, and macroeconomic and trade pressures [0000050863-26-000011:0070][0000050863-26-000011:0071].
findings: The transactions eliminate Intel's contractual rights to receive future grant funds under the commercial CHIPS Act and Secure Enclave agreements, converting that funding into common stock investments by the U.S. government [0000050863-26-000011:0069].

Issuing shares to the U.S. government at a discount to the current market price dilutes existing stockholders, and further dilution could follow if the conditions to the warrant are triggered and it is exercised [0000050863-26-000011:0069].

The U.S. government has agreed to vote its shares as recommended by the board of directors, which reduces the voting influence of other stockholders over director selection and stockholder proposals [0000050863-26-000011:0069].

Other branches of the U.S. government could determine that all or part of the transactions were unauthorized, void or voidable, and no agency other than the Department of Commerce has committed to support the transaction [0000050863-26-000011:0069].

Sales outside the U.S. accounted for 70% of revenue for 2025, and having the U.S. government as a significant stockholder could subject the company to additional foreign regulations, such as foreign subsidy laws [0000050863-26-000011:0070].

The company recognized a $755 million charge in the fourth quarter of 2024 for penalties expected in connection with Ireland SCIP construction delays, and its alternative financing arrangements may include penalties if key metrics are not met [0000050863-26-000011:0068].

title: US export controls and licensing for NVIDIA's China and data center products
summary: This community centers on US export controls and licensing rules affecting NVIDIA's data center and China-bound products, including the H20, H200 and GB200 lines [0001045810-25-000209:0034]. Its main linked items are the AI Diffusion IFR, which the USG said in May 2025 it would rescind in favor of a replacement rule with uncertain scope [0001045810-25-000116:0049], and the H20 licensing requirement for China [0001045810-25-000230:0035]. The passages come only from NVIDIA's filings, so the community does not cover AMD or Intel [0001045810-25-000230:0035].
findings: The AI Diffusion IFR would have imposed a worldwide licensing requirement on NVIDIA's most recent data center products, such as the H200, GB200 and GB300 [0001045810-25-000209:0034].

In April 2025 the USG required a license for H20 exports to China, and NVIDIA recorded a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations [0001045810-25-000230:0035].

The earlier 10-Q states that no revenue had been generated and no H20 products shipped under the August 2025 China licenses [0001045810-25-000209:0054]. The later filing reports approximately $50 million of H20 revenue under those licenses [0001045810-25-000230:0035].

USG officials expected the USG to receive 15% of revenue from licensed H20 sales, but no regulation codifying this had been published [0001045810-25-000209:0054]. The later filing describes the expectation as 15% or more of revenue from licensed sales of NVIDIA's products [0001045810-25-000230:0035].

NVIDIA warns that government mandates for chip tracking and throttling could introduce system vulnerabilities and expose it to significant risk and potential liability [0001045810-25-000116:0049]. China's government publicly questioned whether H20 products had built-in vulnerabilities, which discouraged customers from buying them [0001045810-25-000209:0054].

NVIDIA states that its competitive position has been harmed by export controls and could be further harmed if licenses are delayed or denied or if customers buy from competitors [0001045810-25-000116:0049].
If the most widely adopted open-source models are developed or deployed on competitors' platforms, the influence of NVIDIA's platform could weaken [0001045810-25-000116:0029].
The GAIN AI Act passed the Senate in October 2025 within the NDAA and would restrict the administration's ability to adapt the prior export control rules [0001045810-25-000230:0035].

title: NVIDIA export controls, AI restrictions and regulatory scrutiny
summary: This community covers NVIDIA's exposure to export controls, sanctions and AI-related restrictions, along with the regulatory inquiries it faces in several jurisdictions [0001045810-25-000023:0040]. The passages describe how these controls could limit sales to China and other markets, affect NVIDIA AI cloud services, and interact with the commitments made in the Mellanox acquisition [0001045810-25-000023:0040]. They also describe competition inquiries from the French Competition Authority and from regulators in the European Union, the United States, the United Kingdom, China and South Korea [0001045810-25-000209:0050]. All the passages come from NVIDIA's filings, and none of them cover AMD or Intel [0001045810-25-000116:0046].
findings: The United States has imposed unilateral worldwide controls restricting GPUs and associated products, and such controls could prohibit NVIDIA from exporting to any or all customers in one or more markets, including China and over 150 countries designated Tier 2 by the January 2025 AI Diffusion IFR [0001045810-25-000023:0040].

NVIDIA states that controls could negatively impact its cost and ability to provide services such as NVIDIA AI cloud services, and could affect the ability of its CSPs and customers to serve end customers even outside China [0001045810-25-000023:0040].

NVIDIA states that the possibility of additional export controls has negatively impacted and may further negatively impact demand for its products, benefiting competitors that offer alternatives less likely to be restricted [0001045810-25-000023:0040].

Regulators in China have inquired about NVIDIA's sales, its efforts to supply the China market, and its fulfillment of the commitments made at the close of the Mellanox acquisition, and are investigating whether compliance with U.S. export controls discriminates unfairly against China customers [0001045810-25-000023:0040].

The French Competition Authority collected information from NVIDIA about its business and competition in the graphics card and cloud service provider market as part of an ongoing inquiry, and NVIDIA has received broad requests for information from competition regulators in several jurisdictions [0001045810-25-000209:0050].

In response to the war in Ukraine, the United States and other jurisdictions imposed sanctions and export controls that blocked NVIDIA products, services and support from entering Russia, Belarus and certain regions of Ukraine, and NVIDIA stopped direct sales to Russia in fiscal year 2023 [0001045810-25-000116:0046].

The EU AI Act became effective on August 1, 2024 and will be fully applicable after a two-year transitional period, and it may affect NVIDIA's ability to train, deploy or release AI models in the EU [0001045810-25-000023:0039].

title: NVIDIA export controls and licensing risk
summary: This community concerns NVIDIA's exposure to U.S. export controls and licensing requirements on AI-related GPUs and chips, which the filings say the government may change at any time [0001045810-26-000021:0044]. The linked members connect those controls to data center GPUs, gaming products, HGX and MGX systems, networking demand, and the company's supply chain [0001045810-25-000023:0015]. The passages are all from NVIDIA's filings and do not discuss AMD or Intel [0001045810-25-000116:0047].
findings: NVIDIA states that the worldwide licensing requirements cover its HGX and MGX systems, and that the listed products, including A100, H100 and B200, are subject to those requirements unless a license exception is available [0001045810-25-000023:0015].

The filings describe the USG as evaluating license requests in a closed process without clear standards or an opportunity for review, and say the NAC process has not resulted in approvals for exports to customers in China [0001045810-24-000264:0057].

NVIDIA says that if the USG expands gaming GPU controls, it may disrupt a significant portion of its supply and distribution chain, and that a substantial portion of its products are warehoused in and distributed from Hong Kong [0001045810-25-000023:0044].

Export controls restricting NVIDIA's ability to sell data center GPUs may also reduce demand for its networking products, and the company says export controls have and are likely to have a disproportionate impact on NVIDIA [0001045810-26-000021:0044].
NVIDIA's supply chain is currently concentrated in the Asia-Pacific region, and new or changed export controls could limit alternative manufacturing locations [0001045810-25-000023:0015].

NVIDIA states that its competitive position has been harmed by existing export controls and may be further harmed by further changes, including if customers purchase from competitors [0001045810-24-000124:0051].

The filings say the USG may impose chip tracking and throttling mechanisms that could disable or impair GPUs, and that such government mandates could introduce system vulnerabilities and expose NVIDIA to liability [0001045810-26-000021:0044].

Regulators in China are investigating whether complying with U.S. export controls discriminates unfairly against customers in the China market, and NVIDIA says penalties could follow if it fails to fulfill commitments made at the close of the Mellanox acquisition [0001045810-25-000116:0047].

title: NVIDIA macroeconomic, trade and export-control risks
summary: This community groups NVIDIA risk disclosures on macroeconomic conditions, trade policy and export controls, and its U.S. manufacturing and AI investments [0001045810-25-000023:0063]. Its members tie macroeconomic factors such as tariffs, inflation and supply chain constraints to results of operations, particularly demand for products [0001045810-25-000230:0036]. The filings also link the AI Diffusion IFR replacement and the GAIN AI Act to the risk of new restrictions on NVIDIA products [0001045810-25-000209:0035] [0001045810-25-000230:0036].
findings: Global trade policies, including export controls and tariffs, have added complexity and increased costs throughout the supply chain, and these challenges are likely to persist [0001045810-25-000230:0036].

In May 2025 the USG said it would rescind the AI Diffusion IFR and implement a replacement rule whose scope, timing and requirements remain uncertain, and which may add license requirements with a material impact on the business [0001045810-25-000209:0035].

In October 2025 the Senate passed the GAIN AI Act, which would restrict changes to the Biden Administration's export control rules and could let private U.S. persons review and overturn licensing decisions [0001045810-25-000230:0036].
The supply chain is currently concentrated in the Asia-Pacific region, and new or changed export controls could limit alternative manufacturing locations [0001045810-25-000023:0063].

The company is increasing U.S.-based manufacturing, but its ability to do so depends on the domestic manufacturing ecosystem's capacity to ramp production to the required volume on a timely basis [0001045810-25-000230:0036].

Open-source foundation models could reduce demand for the company's products and services if deployed on competitors' platforms, because open-source AI depends on developer adoption [0001045810-26-000021:0062].
In fiscal year 2026 the company invested $17.5 billion in private companies and infrastructure funds, and many of these investments are illiquid and non-marketable [0001045810-26-000021:0062].

title: NVIDIA export controls and China regulatory risk
summary: This community concerns NVIDIA's exposure to U.S. export controls and Chinese government actions, which the filings tie to demand for its GPUs and networking products [0001045810-25-000230:0063]. Shifting export rules and licensing requirements have led to excess inventory, effective exclusion from China's data center market, and the risk of customers moving to competitors [0001045810-25-000230:0061][0001045810-24-000264:0058]. The passages come from NVIDIA's own filings and describe NVIDIA as the company bearing these risks [0001045810-25-000230:0062].
findings: Export controls restricting data center GPU sales may reduce demand for NVIDIA networking products used in servers containing its GPUs, and the USG may also restrict high-speed network interconnects [0001045810-25-000230:0063].

After an April 9, 2025 license requirement covering H20 circuits, NVIDIA incurred a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 for excess inventory and purchase obligations [0001045810-25-000230:0061].

NVIDIA states it has effectively been foreclosed from competing in China's data center compute market under current rules, which it says will help competitors build larger developer and customer ecosystems [0001045810-25-000230:0061].

China's antitrust regulators published a preliminary finding on September 15, 2025 that NVIDIA's compliance with U.S. export controls, which required degraded products for China, discriminated against China customers and violated the terms of the Mellanox acquisition approval [0001045810-25-000230:0060].

China's government publicly questioned whether H20 products have built-in vulnerabilities, discouraging customers from buying them, and NVIDIA responded that its GPUs do not include such vulnerabilities [0001045810-25-000230:0063].

In August 2025 the USG granted licenses to ship certain H20 products to China-based customers, but NVIDIA has generated about $50 million in H20 revenue under those licenses, and USG officials expect 15% or more of licensed sales revenue, which has not been codified in a regulation [0001045810-25-000230:0062].

NVIDIA says export controls may encourage customers outside China to design out U.S. semiconductors and may lead overseas governments to ask customers to buy from competitors instead of NVIDIA [0001045810-24-000264:0058].

NVIDIA depends on consistent supply from overseas partners, especially in Taiwan and South Korea, and new restrictions that affect supply from those places would negatively affect its business and financial results [0001045810-25-000230:0064].

title: NVIDIA market platforms, products and product-transition risk
summary: This community centers on NVIDIA's four market platforms (Data Center, Gaming, Professional Visualization and Automotive) and the products tied to them, with product-transition and supply risks linked to those platforms [0001045810-24-000264:0034]. The members come only from NVIDIA filings, and the relationships connect named products such as Hopper, GeForce RTX, RTX PRO GPUs and DRIVE Hyperion to their platforms [0001045810-25-000023:0008]. Several risk factors, including export controls, Chinese restrictions and supply constraints, are linked to these platforms [0001045810-24-000316:0051].
findings: NVIDIA says it may be in various stages of transitioning the architectures of its Data Center, Gaming, Professional Visualization and Automotive products, and that this can reduce or create volatility in revenue [0001045810-24-000316:0051].
The filings say supply and capacity commitments may exceed demand, which can lead to inventory provisions or impairments [0001045810-24-000316:0051].
Data Center revenue was up 154% from a year ago, driven by demand for the Hopper GPU computing platform for training and inferencing of large language models [0001045810-24-000264:0034].
Gaming revenue was up 16% from a year ago, reflecting higher sales of GeForce RTX 40 Series GPUs and game console SOCs [0001045810-24-000264:0034].

Professional Visualization revenue was $427 million in the first quarter of fiscal 2025, up 45% from a year ago, and the segment introduced RTX 500 and 1000 laptop GPUs, RTX A400 and A1000 GPUs, and NVIDIA Omniverse Cloud APIs [0001045810-24-000124:0031].
Automotive customers such as Lucid and IM Motors use the NVIDIA DRIVE Orin platform, and BYD, XPENG and others will adopt its successor, NVIDIA DRIVE Thor [0001045810-24-000124:0031].

In August 2022 the USG announced licensing requirements affecting exports to China and Russia of NVIDIA A100 and H100 integrated circuits, DGX systems and boards that incorporate them [0001045810-25-000023:0061].

title: NVIDIA software platforms, AI products and gaming tools
summary: This community centers on NVIDIA's software and accelerated computing products, including CUDA, NVIDIA AI Enterprise with NIM, NeMo and AI Blueprints, Omniverse, DRIVE, and GeForce and RTX gaming tools [0001045810-26-000021:0009][0001045810-25-000023:0011]. The filings describe these as parts of NVIDIA's full-stack platform, with CUDA and its acceleration libraries as the software foundation [0001045810-26-000021:0007]. Its risk-factor member concerns NVIDIA's ability to meet evolving industry needs and to earn revenue from new offerings such as DGX Cloud and standalone software [0001045810-25-000023:0021]. The one AMD passage in the set describes that company's segments rather than any of these products [0000002488-26-000018:0100].
findings: NVIDIA AI Enterprise includes NIM, NeMo and AI Blueprints, which help enterprises build, optimize and deploy AI agents while preserving privacy [0001045810-26-000021:0009].

NVIDIA reported over 7.5 million developers using CUDA and its other software tools in the later filing, up from over 5.9 million in the earlier one [0001045810-26-000021:0009][0001045810-25-000023:0010].

NVIDIA unveiled the Rubin platform in fiscal 2026, with production shipments expected in the second half of fiscal 2027 and up to a 10x reduction in cost per token compared to Blackwell [0001045810-26-000021:0007].
NVIDIA introduced NVLink Fusion in fiscal 2026 to let hyperscalers and custom ASIC designers integrate custom CPUs and XPUs with its platform [0001045810-26-000021:0007].

DRIVE is marketed for autonomous and electric vehicles through partnerships with automotive OEMs, tier-1 suppliers and startups [0001045810-25-000023:0011]. The DRIVE AGX hardware runs an in-vehicle operating system called DRIVE OS [0001045810-26-000021:0009].
NVIDIA warns that its standalone software offerings, including NVIDIA AI Enterprise, Omniverse and DRIVE, may not succeed and may not generate significant revenue [0001045810-25-000023:0021].
GeForce Experience optimizes a gamer's PC settings and enables recording and sharing of gameplay, and Tensor Cores are included in all RTX-class GPUs [0001045810-25-000023:0010].

Omniverse is described as real-time 3D design collaboration and virtual world simulation software, and NVIDIA's vGPU and GeForce NOW platforms extend graphics applications to almost any device through the cloud [0001045810-25-000023:0011].

title: NVIDIA segments, products and customer revenue concentration
summary: This community centers on NVIDIA's two reportable segments, Compute & Networking and Graphics, and the products each one includes [0001045810-24-000264:0027]. Its risk side concerns revenue concentrated among a limited number of direct and indirect customers, notably Customer A and Customer B, and the filings say this trend may continue [0001045810-25-000209:0039]. All the passages concern NVIDIA, and none concern AMD or Intel [0001045810-25-000023:0006].
findings: For the second quarter of fiscal year 2026, sales to Customer A represented 23% of total revenue and sales to Customer B represented 16%, both attributable to the Compute & Networking segment [0001045810-25-000209:0039].
For the first half of fiscal year 2026, Customer A represented 20% of total revenue and Customer B represented 15%, both attributable to the Compute & Networking segment [0001045810-25-000209:0039].

Data Center networking revenue grew 79% year over year compared to the first half of fiscal year 2025, driven by NVLink compute fabric for GB200 and GB300 systems and the ramp of XDR InfiniBand products [0001045810-25-000209:0039].

A $4.5 billion charge for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 partially offset the growth in Compute & Networking segment operating income for the first half [0001045810-25-000209:0039].

The Compute & Networking segment includes Jetson for robotics and other embedded platforms and DGX Cloud computing services, while the Graphics segment includes Quadro/NVIDIA RTX GPUs and Omniverse Enterprise software [0001045810-24-000264:0027].
In the three months ended July 28, 2024, Compute & Networking revenue was 26,446 compared with 3,594 for Graphics [0001045810-24-000264:0027].

Indirect customers primarily purchase NVIDIA products through system integrators and distributors, and indirect customer revenue is an estimate that may differ from actual results [0001045810-25-000209:0039].

title: NVIDIA demand forecasting, supply chain and product transition risk
summary: This community covers NVIDIA risk factors about estimating demand, managing long manufacturing lead times and supply, and transitioning product architectures such as Blackwell [0001045810-25-000230:0052] [0001045810-25-000230:0054]. The filings tie these risks to inventory provisions, prepaid and non-cancellable purchase commitments, and reliance on suppliers, contract manufacturers and assembly partners [0001045810-25-000230:0053] [0001045810-25-000023:0024].
findings: NVIDIA's gross margins in the second quarter of fiscal year 2025 were negatively impacted by inventory provisions for low-yielding Blackwell material [0001045810-25-000230:0054]. The company had also executed a change to the Blackwell GPU mask to improve production yield [0001045810-24-000264:0050].

If NVIDIA overestimates customer demand, it may be unable to reduce inventory or purchase commitments, and it has written down inventory, incurred cancellation penalties and recorded impairments [0001045810-25-000230:0052].
If NVIDIA underestimates demand, its foundry partners may lack lead time or capacity, which could damage customer relationships and cause loss of revenue and market share [0001045810-24-000264:0050].

NVIDIA is increasing its supply and capacity purchases from existing and new suppliers, which adds complexity in managing multiple suppliers with variations in production planning, execution and logistics [0001045810-25-000230:0053].

The filings say the availability of data centers, energy and capital is crucial to customers' AI infrastructure buildout, and expanding energy capacity is a complex, multi-year process; less-capitalized companies may struggle to finance large-scale projects [0001045810-25-000230:0053].

title: AMD's ZT Systems acquisition and sale, OpenAI deal, and China MI308 exposure
summary: This community centers on AMD's acquisition of ZT Systems, the later sale of its manufacturing business to Sanmina Corporation, and AMD's OpenAI product agreement [0000002488-26-000018:0072]. The passages describe only AMD, so the community concerns AMD rather than NVIDIA or Intel [0000002488-26-000018:0005]. AMD's risk factors tie these deals to acquisition, integration and government-approval risks [0000002488-25-000012:0053].
findings: AMD completed the acquisition of ZT Systems on March 31, 2025, paying $3.2 billion in cash and issuing 8,335,849 shares of common stock [0000002488-25-000166:0030].

On October 27, 2025, AMD completed the sale of the ZT Manufacturing Business to Sanmina for 1,151,052 Sanmina shares and $2.4 billion in cash, with up to $450 million more contingent on certain conditions [0000002488-25-000166:0030]. AMD retained the ZT Design Business and says Sanmina will be its preferred partner for manufacturing capabilities [0000002488-26-000018:0072].

New U.S. export restrictions on certain semiconductors to China led to about $800 million in MI308 inventory and related charges in the second quarter of fiscal 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0072]. About $360 million of those charges was later reversed after AMD began shipping under U.S. licenses [0000002488-26-000018:0072].

AMD states that MI308 sales into China depend on customer demand, China's import control rules and its ability to obtain licenses, and it recorded no MI308 China-based customer revenue in the quarter ended September 27, 2025 [0000002488-25-000166:0030].

AMD's risk factors warn that acquisitions and joint ventures may not deliver the expected benefits and may require share issuance, debt or write-downs [0000002488-25-000012:0053]. AMD risk factors: ZT Systems deal, worldwide operations, litigation and environmental rules
summary: This community is a set of risk factors from one AMD filing covering the pending ZT Systems acquisition, worldwide operations, tax, litigation, environmental rules, personnel and stock price [0000002488-24-000163:0038]. The acquisition risks include the possibility that the deal is not completed, a $300 million termination fee in certain cases, and difficulty divesting ZT Systems' manufacturing business [0000002488-24-000163:0070]. The filing also names Intel, whose pricing and incentive practices AMD says have in the past lowered its unit sales and average selling price [0000002488-24-000163:0038].
findings: AMD relies on third-party wafer foundries in the United States, Europe and Asia, and nearly all product assembly and final testing is performed at third-party facilities in China, Malaysia and Taiwan [0000002488-24-000163:0071]. International sales were 72% of net revenue for the three months ended September 28, 2024 [0000002488-24-000163:0071].

Geopolitical changes between China and Taiwan could disrupt AMD's Taiwan-based third-party wafer foundries, and an April 2024 earthquake in Taiwan affected the area where those foundries are located [0000002488-24-000163:0072].

If the ZT Systems acquisition is not completed, AMD may incur acquisition costs it cannot recover, and it would have to pay ZT Systems a $300 million termination fee in certain circumstances tied to failure to obtain required regulatory approvals [0000002488-24-000163:0070].

AMD accounts for the Xilinx, Pensando and Silo AI acquisitions as the accounting acquirer under ASC 805, and it recorded significant goodwill and intangible assets from them that must be tested for impairment [0000002488-24-000163:0070].

AMD has been named a responsible party at three Superfund sites in Sunnyvale, California, and has entered into settlement agreements with other responsible parties on two of the related cleanup orders [0000002488-24-000163:0063].

AMD has been subject to certain claims concerning federal securities laws and corporate governance, and because its products are used by consumers, it may face product liability and consumer class actions [0000002488-24-000163:0062].
AMD has an approved stock repurchase program of up to $12 billion of common stock, and $4.9 billion remained available for repurchases as of September 28, 2024 [0000002488-24-000163:0073].

title: AMD's Silo AI and ZT Systems acquisitions and related risks
summary: This community centers on AMD's acquisitions of Silo AI Oy and ZT Group Int'l (ZT Systems), along with the risk factors that AMD's filings attach to acquisitions and financing [0000002488-24-000163:0068]. findings: AMD's Silo AI purchase was an all-cash transaction of $665 million, with a net purchase consideration of $553 million and $577 million allocated to goodwill [0000002488-24-000163:0012].

AMD would owe a $300 million termination fee if the deal is not completed by August 17, 2025, subject to two automatic extensions [0000002488-24-000163:0012].

Completion of the ZT Systems acquisition depends on receipt of required government consents and approvals, and AMD cannot assure that these will be obtained in time [0000002488-24-000163:0069]. AMD expects the deal to close in the first half of 2025 [0000002488-24-000163:0069].

title: Supply chain, gray market and operational risk factors
summary: The passages are risk-factor text from a single filing, accession 0000002488-24-000163, and they do not name the company that filed it [0000002488-24-000163:0055]. They cover supply-chain efficiency and third-party logistics, gray market diversion, product defects and compatibility, and reliance on internal and information systems [0000002488-24-000163:0056]. The members are risk-factor headings, so their links rest on shared subject matter within the same filing rather than on stated relationships [0000002488-24-000163:0054].
findings: The company relies on its supply chain for manufacturing, distribution and fulfillment, and if it cannot consistently deliver the right products on time, customers may reduce the quantities they order [0000002488-24-000163:0056].

The company relies on third-party providers to operate its regional distribution centers and transport its products, and it cannot guarantee that these providers will perform on time under their contracts [0000002488-24-000163:0056].

Gray market diversion creates shadow inventory that is not visible to the company, which makes demand harder to forecast, and heavily discounted gray market products compete with authorized channels and pressure margins [0000002488-24-000163:0056].
Products bought on the gray market may be counterfeit, substandard, altered, damaged or used items represented as new, which can cause customer satisfaction problems [0000002488-24-000163:0056].

Defects in complex products could lead to lost market acceptance, recall and replacement costs, inventory write-downs and litigation, and the company may have difficulty identifying end customers of defective products in the field [0000002488-24-000163:0055].

Products may not be fully compatible with some or all industry-standard software and hardware, and the mere announcement of an incompatibility problem could hurt the business [0000002488-24-000163:0055].

The company's agreements with distributors and AIB partners are non-exclusive and can be terminated for convenience, and they permit these partners to offer competitors' products [0000002488-24-000163:0054].

A more distributed IT environment makes it harder to maintain visibility and control over internal and external users, and the company's systems may be vulnerable to cyberattacks and data breaches [0000002488-24-000163:0055].

Natural disasters and climate-related events could disrupt operations, and the company states that its headquarters and some facilities are in areas susceptible to earthquakes, tsunamis, wildfires and other disasters [0000002488-24-000163:0057].

title: NVIDIA demand, supply and manufacturing risk factors
findings: NVIDIA says it has previously experienced lead times of more than 12 months and has paid premiums, provided deposits, and entered into long-term supply and capacity commitments that have increased its product costs [0001045810-26-000021:0022].

Overestimating demand can leave NVIDIA unable to reduce supply commitments, which has led to write-downs, cancellation penalties, impairments, and lower average selling prices [0001045810-26-000021:0022].

Underestimating demand is a risk if foundry partners and contract manufacturers cannot increase production in time, and component shortages can have a broader revenue impact because its products form part of a complex data center buildout [0001045810-26-000021:0022].

NVIDIA states that the availability of data centers, energy, and capital for customer buildouts is crucial, and that shortages of these resources could delay deployments and reduce its future revenue [0001045810-26-000021:0023].
NVIDIA says it may experience delays or difficulties in scaling its expanded U.S.-based manufacturing as planned, which could affect its ability to meet demand [0001045810-26-000021:0024].

Frequent product transitions can cause customers to delay purchases of prior architectures, and NVIDIA cites inventory provisions for low-yielding Blackwell material as a reason its gross margins were negatively affected in the second quarter of fiscal year 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0024].

Demand is hard to forecast because GPUs are used for varied applications, and cryptocurrency mining has caused inconsistent spikes and drops in demand, with the Ethereum 2.0 merge reducing mining use and creating aftermarket GPU sales [0001045810-26-000021:0025].

NVIDIA depends on third-party foundries and subcontractors and does not assemble, test, or package its products, which reduces its control over quantity, quality, yields, and delivery schedules [0001045810-26-000021:0025].

title: Groq license arrangement and NVIDIA risk factors
summary: This community centers on NVIDIA's non-exclusive intellectual property license agreement with Groq, Inc., which NVIDIA's filing describes as entered into in December 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0102]. The community also links that agreement to a risk factor warning that the licensed technology may not yield results or recoverable costs [0001045810-26-000021:0020]. Two other NVIDIA risk factors, on data privacy laws and on provisions that could delay a change in control, are grouped here but are not tied to Groq in the passages provided [0001045810-26-000021:0020].
findings: NVIDIA entered into a non-exclusive license agreement with Groq, Inc. for its language processing unit technology and hired certain Groq employees, but did not purchase any customer contracts, existing products, or equity interests [0001045810-26-000021:0102].
Total consideration for the Groq arrangement was $13.0 billion paid at closing plus $4 billion, inclusive of imputed interest, payable within one year [0001045810-26-000021:0102].

NVIDIA recorded $14.4 billion of goodwill and a $2.5 billion developed technology intangible asset with a five-year useful life from the Groq transaction, with the goodwill recorded in the Compute & Networking reporting unit [0001045810-26-000021:0102].

NVIDIA warns that incorporating the Groq-licensed technology requires significant engineering effort, may not produce the desired results or customer adoption, and may leave it unable to recover the associated costs [0001045810-26-000021:0020].

Cash used in investing activities rose in fiscal year 2026 compared to fiscal year 2025, primarily due to higher equity investment purchases and the execution of the non-exclusive license agreement with Groq [0001045810-26-000021:0070].

title: VLSI patent litigation against Intel and the Finjan license defense
summary: This community centers on VLSI's patent infringement suits against Intel, including three Texas cases, two Chinese cases, and a Delaware suit, and it concerns Intel rather than NVIDIA or AMD [0000050863-25-000109:0037] [0000050863-25-000074:0033]. Intel's main defense is that it is licensed to VLSI's patents through its license agreement with Finjan, which was acquired by Fortress Investments [0000050863-25-000179:0044]. Intel's Chinese subsidiaries are named alongside Intel as defendants in the Shenzhen and Shanghai cases [0000050863-25-000179:0044].
findings: VLSI filed three infringement suits against Intel in April 2019 in the Western District of Texas, accusing various processors of infringing eight patents VLSI acquired from NXP [0000050863-25-000109:0037].

In the first Texas case, the jury awarded VLSI $1.5 billion and $675 million, and in April 2022 the court entered final judgment of $2.2 billion in damages plus about $162 million in interest [0000050863-25-000109:0037].

In December 2023 the Federal Circuit reversed the infringement finding tied to the $675 million award, affirmed infringement on the $1.5 billion patent, and vacated that damages award [0000050863-25-000109:0037].

In the third Texas case, the jury found the remaining patent valid and infringed and awarded VLSI about $949 million, and in May 2025 a jury returned a verdict in Intel's favor on a factual question about the license defense [0000050863-25-000179:0044].
In the second Texas case, the jury found that Intel does not infringe the asserted patents, against VLSI's request for about $3.0 billion [0000050863-24-000124:0034].
In the Shenzhen case, the CNIPA invalidated every claim of the asserted patent in September 2023 and the trial court dismissed VLSI's case in November 2023 [0000050863-25-000074:0033].

Intel sued VLSI in the District of Delaware in July 2024 seeking a finding that Intel is licensed to VLSI's patents, and in December 2024 the court stayed that case until May 31, 2025 [0000050863-25-000074:0033].

As of December 28, 2024, Intel had accrued a charge of approximately $1.0 billion related to the VLSI litigation, and it said it could not reasonably estimate losses above that amount [0000050863-25-000009:0160].

title: R2 Semiconductor patent litigation and August 2024 settlements
summary: This community covers Intel's patent litigation with R2 Semiconductor, which asserts one European patent against Intel's Ice Lake, Tiger Lake, Alder Lake and Ice Lake Server processors in courts in the UK, Germany, France and Italy [0000050863-24-000124:0035]. Customers including Dell, HP, HPE, Fujitsu and Amazon Web Services are named in the suits, and Intel is indemnifying and defending its customers [0000050863-24-000124:0035]. In August 2024 Intel entered into three confidential agreements with R2, Third Point (the controlling shareholder) and TRGP Capital (a third party funding the lawsuits) to resolve the injunction enforcement risk and related litigation [0000050863-24-000149:0039].
findings: The Dusseldorf Regional Court found in February 2024 that Intel's processors infringe and issued an injunction and recall order against Intel and its customers [0000050863-24-000124:0035].
Intel recorded a charge of $780 million in the second quarter of 2024 related to the three confidential settlement agreements with R2, Third Point and TRGP [0000050863-24-000149:0034].

The earlier filing described the three agreements as still under negotiation when the $780 million charge was recorded [0000050863-24-000124:0036]. The later filing says Intel expects to pay an aggregate $780 million across the three agreements [0000050863-25-000009:0161].
The UK High Court of Justice found the UK part of R2's European patent invalid in July 2024 [0000050863-24-000124:0035].

R2 filed a patent infringement action in Paris in April 2024 against Intel and its customers Dell, HP and HPE, and Intel and its customers filed a nullity action against the patent in France [0000050863-24-000124:0036].

Intel Corporation Italia filed an action in Milan in March 2024 seeking an order that Intel processors do not infringe R2's patent, and R2 responded in June 2024 with counterclaims of infringement against the same processors [0000050863-24-000124:0035].
Third Point is identified in the filings as the controlling shareholder and is one of the three counterparties to the August 2024 agreements [0000050863-24-000149:0039].

title: Intel EC competition fines and Spectre/Meltdown litigation
summary: This community concerns Intel's long-running European Commission competition matter and the Spectre and Meltdown security-vulnerability litigation, both reported in its legal proceedings [0000050863-24-000076:0027] [0000050863-24-000076:0028]. The EC matter runs from a 2009 finding and €1.1 billion fine through a 2022 partial annulment and a 2023 €376 million fine [0000050863-24-000076:0027] [0000050863-24-000124:0031] [0000050863-24-000149:0035]. The Spectre and Meltdown matters are consumer class actions in the US and Canada, and an Argentina class action that ended in February 2024, and Intel says it cannot estimate potential losses from them [0000050863-24-000076:0028] [0000050863-24-000149:0035].
findings: The EC found in 2009 that Intel used unfair business practices in violation of Article 82 of the EC Treaty and Article 54 of the European Economic Area Agreement, and it imposed a €1.1 billion fine that Intel paid in the third quarter of 2009 [0000050863-24-000076:0027].

In January 2022 the General Court annulled the EC's 2009 findings on rebates and the €1.1 billion fine, which was returned to Intel in February 2022, but it did not annul the finding that Intel made payments to prevent sales of specific rival products [0000050863-24-000124:0031].
In October 2024 the Court of Justice dismissed the EC's appeal of the General Court's rebates findings, upholding the General Court's judgment [0000050863-24-000149:0035].

In September 2023 the EC imposed a €376 million ($401 million) fine based on its payments finding, Intel has appealed the decision, and Intel has accrued a charge for the fine [0000050863-24-000149:0035].
As of December 27, 2025, Intel had accrued liabilities of $311 million, including revaluation effects and accrued interest, related to the EC-imposed fine [0000050863-26-000011:0171].

In April 2022 Intel applied to the General Court for an order requiring the EC to pay approximately €593 million in default interest on the original €1.1 billion fine, and in November 2024 the EC paid approximately €516 million in settlement of those applications [0000050863-25-000009:0156].

US consumer class actions over Spectre and Meltdown were consolidated in the US District Court for the District of Oregon, which entered final judgment in favor of Intel in July 2022, and the Ninth Circuit affirmed that judgment in November 2023, ending the litigation [0000050863-24-000076:0028].

A November 2023 consumer class action over the Downfall vulnerability was dismissed by the district court in August 2024, and plaintiffs filed an amended complaint in September 2024 that Intel moved to dismiss in October 2024 [0000050863-24-000149:0035].

title: EireOg and Media Content Protection patent suits against Intel customers
summary: This community covers patent suits in Intel's filings, mainly Eire Og Innovations' eleven Texas complaints and the Media Content Protection case, both aimed at Intel and its customers [0000050863-26-000011:0177][0000050863-26-000011:0178]. Intel indemnifies Acer, AWS, Cisco, Dell, HPE, HPI, IBM, Lenovo and Oracle against the Eire Og claims, while the Media Content Protection case names Dell, HP Inc., Lenovo and LG Electronics as customers whose products carry the accused Intel circuits [0000050863-26-000011:0177][0000050863-26-000011:0178]. The community concerns Intel, although the Eire Og complaints also accuse AMD CPUs [0000050863-26-000011:0177].
findings: Intel is indemnifying Acer, Amazon Web Services, Cisco, Dell, HPE, HPI, IBM, Lenovo and Oracle over Intel CPUs accused of infringing four patents [0000050863-26-000011:0177].

EireOg Innovations Ltd. has filed eleven separate complaints since April 2024 in the Eastern and Western Districts of Texas against Intel and AMD customers, seeking compensatory damages and future royalties [0000050863-26-000011:0177].
Philips sold the asserted patents to Media Content Protection in July 2024, and MCP substituted in as plaintiff, seeking $66 million to $398 million in royalty damages [0000050863-26-000011:0178].
In November 2025 the court granted Intel's summary judgment of invalidity on both patents, a final judgment for Intel followed in December 2025, and MCP has appealed [0000050863-26-000011:0178].
Philips alleged that Intel digital video circuits infringed two of its patents, including circuits in products sold by Dell, HP Inc., Lenovo and LG Electronics [0000050863-26-000011:0178].
In September 2025 EireOg moved to dismiss its claims against Acer and HPI without prejudice, and AWS's motion to dismiss the amended complaint was denied in July 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0177].
Intel states it cannot make a reasonable estimate of the potential loss or range of losses from the Eire Og matters [0000050863-26-000011:0177].

title: AMD risk factors: cybersecurity, foundry supply and export exposure
summary: This community groups AMD risk factors from its annual filing, covering cybersecurity, product security, third-party manufacturing, customer concentration and export controls [0000002488-25-000166:0043]. Some of the risks overlap, since both the product security and the cyberattack risks state that vulnerabilities could harm AMD's brand and reputation [0000002488-25-000166:0054][0000002488-25-000166:0055]. The passages concern AMD only and state no other links among these risk factors [0000002488-25-000166:0055].
findings: AMD states that it relies on TSMC for all wafers for microprocessor and GPU products at 7 nm or smaller nodes, and primarily on GLOBALFOUNDRIES for those at larger nodes [0000002488-25-000166:0050].
AMD expects a small number of customers to continue to account for a substantial part of its revenue, so the loss of a key customer would materially affect its business [0000002488-25-000166:0049].

After an April 2025 U.S. license requirement restricted exports of its AMD Instinct MI308 products to China, AMD incurred approximately $800 million in inventory and related charges in the second quarter of 2025 [0000002488-25-000166:0057].

AMD's semi-custom SoC revenue consists of non-recurring engineering fees and sales tied to third parties' products, and AMD has no control over those third parties' marketing efforts [0000002488-25-000166:0054].
AMD describes cyber threats ranging from hackers and insiders to ransom gangs and state-sponsored attackers, and warns that AI tools may enable more sophisticated attacks [0000002488-25-000166:0055].
A large portion of AMD's quarterly sales has historically been made in the last month of the quarter, which makes revenue prediction difficult [0000002488-25-000166:0049].

title: AMD operational and product risk factors
summary: This community is made up of AMD risk factors from the Item 1A section of its annual filing, covering product defects, compatibility, supply chain, outsourced logistics, gray market sales, internal information systems and climate change [0000002488-25-000047:0032]. The members are tied to one another only by the shared risk-factor category, since the community records no relationships among them [0000002488-25-000047:0033]. findings: AMD warns that its products may not be fully compatible with some or all industry-standard software and hardware, and that even the announcement of an incompatibility problem could have a material adverse effect on its business [0000002488-25-000047:0050].

title: AMD third-party dependencies: Microsoft, motherboards, distributors and IP
summary: This community is a cluster of AMD risk factors about reliance on outside parties for software, hardware components, distribution and intellectual property [0000002488-25-000047:0048]. The passages describe AMD's Instinct MI308 product and its x86 products competing against Intel's x86 instruction set, which places this community in AMD's filing [0000002488-25-000047:0047] [0000002488-25-000047:0048]. The member risk factors appear together in one risk section, and the passages cite no explicit relationships among them [0000002488-25-000047:0049].
findings: AMD says its ability to innovate beyond the x86 instruction set controlled by Intel depends partly on Microsoft designing its operating systems to run on or support its x86 products [0000002488-25-000047:0048]. It also says that if Microsoft does not certify a driver, or AMD otherwise loses support from Microsoft or other software vendors, its ability to market x86 products would be materially adversely affected [0000002488-25-000047:0048].

AMD depends on third-party companies for the design, manufacture and supply of motherboards, graphics cards, software, memory and other components [0000002488-25-000047:0048]. It also notes that its microprocessors are not designed to function with motherboards and chipsets built for Intel microprocessors [0000002488-25-000047:0048].

AMD sells directly and through third-party distributors and AIB partners under agreements that can generally be terminated for convenience on prior notice, and these agreements are non-exclusive and let partners offer competitors' products [0000002488-25-000047:0049].

AMD's agreements with AIB partners protect their inventory against price reductions, so a significant decline in product prices would reduce AMD's revenue and gross margin [0000002488-25-000047:0049].

AMD relies on third-party intellectual property and development and testing tools, and if that intellectual property becomes unavailable or fails to meet requirements, its business could be materially adversely affected [0000002488-25-000047:0048].

AMD states that its information technology systems, and those of third-party IT providers or business partners, may be vulnerable to disruption from events such as cyberattacks, data breaches and system failures [0000002488-25-000047:0049].

AMD says customers may cancel standard-product orders more than 30 days before shipment without significant fees, and a new U.S. license requirement for certain exports to China restricts its AMD Instinct MI308 product [0000002488-25-000047:0047]. AMD expects the restriction may result in charges of approximately $800 million in inventory and related reserves [0000002488-25-000047:0047].

title: AMD export controls on China and D5 countries, and climate-related supply risk
summary: This community concerns AMD's export-control and climate-change risk factors, which recur across several of its 10-K and 10-Q filings and name AMD Instinct integrated circuits and Versal FPGAs as affected products [0000002488-25-000012:0043]. The export side covers BIS controls on China and D5 countries, the April 2025 license requirement for the MI308, and a possible U.S. government revenue share on licensed MI308 sales [0000002488-25-000166:0063][0000002488-25-000166:0064]. The climate side links physical disruption and new climate regulation to supply chain delays and contractual disputes [0000002488-26-000018:0041]. Every passage comes from an AMD filing, and none names NVIDIA or Intel [0000002488-25-000012:0042].
findings: The October 2023 BIS requirements prevent AMD from shipping certain Instinct integrated circuits and Versal FPGAs to China, or to customers outside the United States whose ultimate parent is in a D5 country, without a license [0000002488-25-000012:0043]. Certain Versal FPGAs also require a Notified Advanced Computing notification to BIS 25 days before shipment [0000002488-25-000047:0053].

AMD incurred approximately $800 million in inventory and related charges in the second quarter of 2025 because of the April 2025 license requirement, which covers its MI308 products [0000002488-25-000166:0063]. AMD has been granted some licenses to ship MI308 products to certain China-based customers, but sales depend on customer demand, China's import rules and its ability to obtain licenses [0000002488-25-000166:0063].

In August 2025 U.S. government officials expressed an expectation of receiving 15% of revenue from licensed MI308 sales to China, but no regulation has been published to establish this [0000002488-25-000166:0064]. Any such request could lead to litigation and harm AMD's competitive position [0000002488-25-000166:0064].

BIS announced in May 2025 its intention to rescind the January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule and issue replacement rules [0000002488-25-000166:0064]. The replacement rules may require new export licenses, delay shipments or require changes to AMD's compliance processes and product designs [0000002488-25-000166:0064].

AMD is subject to the Export Administration Regulations, which restrict exports of certain products and technologies to countries including China, Russia and Belarus [0000002488-26-000018:0041]. These restrictions may limit AMD's ability to sell certain products in those markets or to certain customers [0000002488-26-000018:0041].

AMD has equity interests in two joint ventures with Higon Information Technology, known as the THATIC JV, and BIS added THATIC and the THATIC JV to the Entity List in June 2019 [0000002488-25-000012:0042]. AMD states that U.S.-China trade relations remain uncertain as more Chinese companies are added to the Entity List [0000002488-25-000012:0042].

AMD states that climate-related disruptions could delay manufacturing or shipping, affect its supply chain, and lead to contractual disputes and increased litigation and costs [0000002488-25-000012:0041]. The long-term effects of climate change on the technology industry are described as unclear but potentially severe [0000002488-25-000012:0041].

Data centers depend on clean water and reliable energy, so power or water shortages could stop customers from expanding data center capacity or from buying AMD products [0000002488-26-000018:0041]. Climate-related carbon taxes and energy regulations may raise AMD's costs, and suppliers' added compliance costs may be passed on to AMD [0000002488-25-000012:0042].

title: AMD ATMP JVs and THATIC JV with Chinese partners
summary: This community concerns AMD's equity joint ventures with Chinese partners: the ATMP JVs, in which AMD holds a 15% interest with affiliates of Tongfu Microelectronics, provide assembly, test, mark and packaging services, while the THATIC JV with Higon Information Technology Co., Ltd. (THATIC) takes licensed AMD intellectual property [0000002488-24-000056:0012]. The Bureau of Industry and Security added THATIC and the THATIC JV to the Entity List in June 2019, and AMD states that it is complying with that designation [0000002488-25-000012:0105]. AMD's risk factors link these ventures to acquisition and integration risk, noting that the ATMP JVs may not fulfill its long-term ATMP requirements and that it may not realize the expected benefits of the THATIC JV [0000002488-24-000056:0061].
findings: AMD's purchases from the ATMP JV were $1.7 billion in each of 2024 and 2023, and amounts payable to the ATMP JV rose from $363 million at December 30, 2023 to $476 million at December 28, 2024 [0000002488-25-000012:0104].

On October 9, 2024, AMD entered into a one-year term loan of $100 million with one of the ATMP JVs, bearing interest at three-month SOFR plus 50 basis points and secured by the JV's receivable balance due from AMD, with the option to extend for up to twelve months [0000002488-25-000012:0104].
In the six months ended June 28, 2025, AMD's purchases from the ATMP JV were $1.0 billion, compared with $839 million in the six months ended June 29, 2024 [0000002488-25-000108:0018].
AMD's carrying value of its ATMP JV investment rose from $99 million at December 30, 2023 to $149 million at December 28, 2024, and to $165 million at June 28, 2025 [0000002488-25-000108:0018].

AMD recognized licensing gains from royalty income under the February 2016 agreement with the THATIC JV of $48 million in 2024 and $34 million in 2023, while the carrying value of its THATIC JV investment was zero [0000002488-25-000012:0105].

AMD warns that if it cannot meet customer demand because of fluctuating or late supply from the ATMP JVs, it could lose sales and suffer a material adverse effect on its business [0000002488-24-000123:0069].

BIS's October 2023 requirements prevent AMD from shipping certain AMD Instinct integrated circuits and certain AMD Versal FPGAs to China, or to customers whose ultimate parent is headquartered in a D5 country, without a license [0000002488-24-000056:0052].

title: Litigation, IP claims, talent and Mobileye impairment risk factors
summary: The risk factors on litigation and IP claims are closely linked, with each one pointing to the others and to the same legal matters [0000050863-26-000011:0081]. Several passages repeat near-identical wording across filing years, so the community is largely one set of risks restated over time [0000050863-25-000009:0067].
findings: The filings warn that an unfavorable litigation outcome can materially harm business, financial condition and results, and may bring monetary damages, fines, or injunctions stopping sales of certain products [0000050863-26-000011:0081].

The filings say non-practicing entities have brought costly suits, including the VLSI and R2 litigation, which have produced significant adverse judgments and settlements, and that a February 2024 R2 injunction and recall order in Germany could have disrupted European business [0000050863-26-000011:0080].

The filings state that third-party licenses needed for products may not be available on commercially reasonable terms or at all, and failure to obtain them could preclude selling certain products [0000050863-26-000011:0081].

The earlier filing cites headcount reductions in 2022 and 2024 [0000050863-25-000009:0069], while the later filing adds reductions in 2025 and CEO transitions in 2025, 2024, 2021 and 2019 [0000050863-26-000011:0082].
The earlier filing says the most recent CEO retired in December 2024 after less than four years and that a search for a new CEO was underway [0000050863-25-000009:0069].

The filings report a $2.8 billion charge in the third quarter of 2024, primarily related to Mobileye goodwill [0000050863-26-000011:0082]. A 1% increase in the discount rate would have produced an additional Mobileye goodwill impairment of about $1.5 billion in that quarter, and further impairment is possible [0000050863-25-000109:0061].

The filings say that loss contingencies may be adjusted as cases develop, and that resolution against the company for more than management's estimates could materially and adversely affect results of operations and financial condition [0000050863-25-000109:0061].
The filings state that the company may have to license some patents for little or no cost under industry standards, which can impair the value of its IP rights [0000050863-26-000011:0080].

title: Cybersecurity risk, supply-chain attacks and data privacy compliance
summary: This community covers Intel's cybersecurity risk disclosures, which tie persistent attack risk to supply-chain exposure and to laws on cybersecurity and data privacy [0000050863-25-000009:0065]. It names SolarWinds Corporation, CrowdStrike and the Habana Labs subsidiary as concrete examples of these risks [0000050863-25-000009:0065]. The passages are Intel's filings, as shown by the reference to Intel directors' cybersecurity experience [0000050863-26-000011:0092].
findings: The filing cites the 2020 compromise of IT infrastructure management software from SolarWinds Corporation and the 2024 CrowdStrike outage as examples of supply-chain risk from widely adopted products [0000050863-25-000009:0065].

Habana Labs, a subsidiary, had its network breached in the fourth quarter of 2020 in connection with a suspected unsuccessful ransomware attack, which resulted in unauthorized third-party access to certain confidential information [0000050863-25-000009:0065].

Failure or perceived failure to comply with cybersecurity and data privacy laws, rules, regulations and standards could require modifying or ceasing operations, substantial costs, legal proceedings including class actions, or governmental investigations [0000050863-25-000009:0065].

The cybersecurity risks are described as significant and persistent, driven by the breadth of geographies and systems to defend, the attractiveness of Intel's systems to threat actors including state-sponsored organizations, and the use of third-party products and components [0000050863-25-000009:0081].

Intel reports having seen an increase in cyberattack volume, frequency and sophistication, and states that it has not yet experienced a cybersecurity incident with a material adverse impact [0000050863-26-000011:0092].
Threat actors are described as using emerging AI technologies to build new hacking tools, exploit vulnerabilities and impersonate authorized individuals [0000050863-25-000009:0065].

Intel expects its foundry business and its cloud computing and SaaS offerings to collect significant amounts of highly sensitive customer data, which may make it a more frequent target of data theft [0000050863-25-000009:0064].

Security vulnerabilities and mitigation techniques can adversely affect results, customer relationships and reputation through costs for updates, inventory write-downs, litigation and lost demand [0000050863-26-000011:0078].

title: IP, cybersecurity and data-privacy risk factors
summary: The passages do not name the company that filed them, and they all come from two filings under a single filer ID, so they do not cover NVIDIA or AMD. [0000050863-26-000011:0079] [0000050863-25-000009:0066] [0000050863-25-000009:0067] [0000050863-26-000011:0080]
findings: The filer warns that cyber attacks are increasing in number, magnitude and sophistication, and that a successful attack could expose proprietary or confidential information or disrupt its supply chain and manufacturing operations [0000050863-26-000011:0079].

The filer says threat actors are using emerging AI tools to build new hacking methods, and that its own adoption of generative AI in internal systems may create new attack methods [0000050863-26-000011:0079].

Noncompliance with cybersecurity, data protection and privacy laws could require the filer to modify or cease operations, incur substantial costs, face class action lawsuits, or pay government fines [0000050863-26-000011:0079].

The filer says theft or misuse of personal data, including data held by vendors, could raise business and security costs and legal defense costs, and that noncompliance could bring monetary penalties, suspension of online services in some countries, and criminal sanctions [0000050863-25-000009:0066].

The filer states it cannot always protect its IP or enforce its IP rights, and that a claim that its IP rights are invalid or licensed to an opponent could be raised when it enforces them [0000050863-25-000009:0066].

Licenses with other companies and participation in industry standards organizations can let competitors use some of the filer's patents, and the filer sometimes must license patents for little or no cost, which may leave it unable to enforce certain patents and impair the value of its IP [0000050863-26-000011:0080].

The filer reports an increase in patent suits by well-funded non-practicing entities, including a February 2024 injunction and recall order obtained by R2 Semiconductor in a German court, and says the VLSI and R2 litigation produced significant adverse judgments and settlements [0000050863-25-000009:0067].

Under IP rights claims, the filer says it could be required to pay damages, stop manufacturing or selling affected products, develop substitutes, or enter costly settlement or license agreements, and that it may indemnify customers against such claims [0000050863-26-000011:0080].

title: Distributor, customer-concentration and strategic-transaction risk factors
