title: Data privacy, AI and cyber regulation risk
summary: This community groups risk-factor language on data privacy, AI, cybersecurity and corporate responsibility rules, naming laws such as the GDPR, U.K. GDPR, CCPA, EU AI Act and NIS2 [0001045810-25-000023:0048]. It also covers cross-border data transfer rules, including Standard Contractual Clauses and China's data localization law with CAC approval [0001045810-26-000021:0050]. The passages come from two filings with different filer IDs, and the text describes the filer's exposure without naming the company [0000002488-24-000163:0051].
findings: The filing says that if it is found not to comply with the GDPR, it could be subject to penalties of up to 20 million euros or 4% of worldwide revenue, whichever is greater [0001045810-25-000023:0048].
Non-compliance with NIS2 may lead to administrative fines of a maximum of 10 million euros or up to 2% of the total worldwide revenue of the preceding fiscal year [0001045810-26-000021:0050].

Data broadly defined as important under China's law, including personal data, may not be transferable outside China without prior assessment and approval by the Cyberspace Administration of China [0001045810-26-000021:0050].
The CCPA provides for substantial fines for intentional violation and created a private right of action for certain data breaches [0001045810-25-000023:0048].

One filing describes the EU AI Act as something that is being considered, while a later filing says the EU AI Act was adopted in 2024 and will be phased in over the next few years [0000002488-24-000123:0065] [0000002488-25-000047:0061].

The filing warns that threat actors can compromise users' access credentials through phishing, vishing, smishing and MFA prompt bombing, and that AI may make attacks more automated and targeted [0000002488-24-000163:0051].

The later filing says California has passed climate reporting requirements that include third-party verification of climate data, and that failure to comply could result in penalties and harm to reputation [0000002488-25-000047:0061].

title: Environmental, conflict minerals, labor, privacy and litigation compliance risks
summary: The 2025 filing names AMD and describes its own government regulation and environmental disclosures [0000002488-25-000012:0017]. The 2024 and 2026 filings describe the same compliance and Superfund themes in the first person, and the 2026 filing states the company's environmental accrual and its remediation obligations [0000002488-26-000018:0019].
findings: AMD says it has been named a responsible party at three Superfund sites in Sunnyvale, California, and is subject to Final Site Clean-up Requirements Orders from the California Regional Water Quality Control Board, with settlement agreements with other responsible parties on two of those orders [0000002488-24-000123:0063].

AMD recorded an estimated environmental liability of approximately $5.9 million for anticipated future remediation costs under the orders, and it has not recorded any potential insurance recoveries [0000002488-26-000018:0019].

The filing says AMD incurs costs to comply with conflict minerals reporting requirements to customers and the SEC, and that customers requiring all components to be certified conflict free may choose a competitor's products if those demands are not met [0000002488-24-000123:0064].

Customers, governments and authorities are focused on eliminating forced labor risks in supply chains, and failure to satisfy customer expectations on forced and trafficked labor policies may lead customers to choose a competitor's product or create enforcement liability [0000002488-24-000123:0064].
Many governments have enacted privacy laws such as the GDPR and CCPA, and non-compliance could bring sanctions, with the GDPR carrying significant fines [0000002488-24-000123:0065].

The filings say environmental laws change frequently and tend to become more stringent over time, with the EU and China restricting lead and other materials in electronic products [0000002488-25-000012:0017]. AMD also states that compliance has not historically had a material impact on its financial condition, earnings or competitive position, but that evolving laws could require significant costs or product design changes [0000002488-26-000018:0019].

AMD is a defendant or plaintiff in various legal actions, including claims about federal securities laws, product liability and consumer class actions, and claims by individuals alleging exposure to substances at former wafer manufacturing facilities [0000002488-24-000123:0062].

title: AMD Sunnyvale Superfund sites and environmental regulation
summary: This community concerns AMD's environmental liabilities from three Superfund sites in Sunnyvale, California, for which AMD says it was named a responsible party [0000002488-25-000012:0018]. The 1991 Final Site Clean-up Requirements Orders from the California Regional Water Quality Control Board relate to those three sites, and AMD has settled some of the orders with other responsible parties [0000002488-26-000018:0018]. The community also covers the broader environmental laws AMD cites, including CERCLA and rules on materials, chemicals, energy and waste [0000002488-26-000018:0019].
findings: AMD states that the Superfund Act can impose strict or, in some circumstances, joint and several liability on current and previous owners or operators of real property, and that persons who arrange for hazardous substances to be sent to contaminated facilities can be liable even if they never owned or operated them [0000002488-25-000012:0018].

AMD computed and recorded an estimated environmental liability of approximately $5.5 million in one filing and approximately $5.9 million in a later filing, without recording any potential insurance recoveries [0000002488-25-000012:0018][0000002488-26-000018:0019].

Under one agreement with another responsible party, that party is responsible for certain offsite contamination, while AMD remains responsible for on-site cleanup and for all remaining costs if the other party does not meet its obligations [0000002488-26-000018:0019].

In the 2025 filing, AMD says it entered settlement agreements with other responsible parties on two of the orders, and those parties assumed most foreseeable costs and the primary role in remediation during the agreement terms [0000002488-25-000012:0018].

AMD reports that it has discovered hazardous material releases to groundwater from former underground tanks since 1981, and that the chemicals released were commonly used in semiconductor wafer fabrication before 1979 [0000002488-25-000012:0018].

AMD says environmental regulations on lead, PFAS, energy efficiency and electronic waste recycling affect its products, and that the scope of these laws is inconsistent, which increases compliance complexity [0000002488-26-000018:0019].

AMD's risk factors state that supplier noncompliance could disrupt supply, and that AMD could be named a potentially responsible party at other Superfund or contaminated sites in the future [0000002488-25-000166:0070].
report:

title: Intel 14A external-customer dependency and manufacturing footprint cuts
summary: This community concerns Intel's leading-edge process roadmap, centered on Intel 14A and its dependence on winning a significant external foundry customer [0000050863-26-000011:0008]. Intel states that if it cannot secure that customer, it may pause or discontinue Intel 14A and successor nodes, which would also affect planned manufacturing facility expansions [0000050863-26-000011:0034].
findings: Intel says that if it is unable to secure a significant external foundry customer for Intel 14A, it may pause or discontinue its pursuit of Intel 14A and successor leading-edge process technologies [0000050863-26-000011:0008].

Intel states that it has few external foundry customers to date, and that Intel 14A may not be economical to develop and manufacture without a significant external customer [0000050863-26-000011:0008] [0000050863-26-000011:0034].

Intel says that any decision to pause or discontinue its pursuit of Intel 14A and successor leading-edge process technologies may be effectively irreversible, given the years of R&D, intellectual property and facility investment involved [0000050863-25-000109:0065].

In 2025 Intel initiated consolidating its Costa Rican assembly and test operations into existing sites in Vietnam and Malaysia, slowed construction of the new Ohio fab, and discontinued planned expansions in Germany and Poland [0000050863-26-000011:0034].

Intel has said that if it discontinued Intel 14A and successor nodes, a majority of its products would still be made in its own facilities on nodes up to Intel 18A-P through at least 2030, and that it would expect to shift manufacturing to third-party foundries, particularly TSMC, for nodes beyond Intel 18A [0000050863-26-000011:0034] [0000050863-26-000011:0008].

Intel Core Ultra Series 3 processors, the first products on Intel 18A, were recently released, and Intel 18A is currently its most advanced leading-edge node [0000050863-26-000011:0034] [0000050863-26-000011:0021].
Intel's Ohio fab and Germany plans were already on hold as of its earlier 2025 filing, and Intel 20A productization was canceled in favor of Intel 18A [0000050863-25-000009:0014].

title: Intel fabs, assembly sites and advanced packaging technologies
summary: This community covers Intel's manufacturing footprint, with production fabs in Oregon, Arizona, Ireland and Israel and assembly and test sites in China, New Mexico, Vietnam and Malaysia [0000050863-26-000011:0022]. It also groups Intel's advanced packaging technologies (EMIB, EMIB-T, Foveros and Foveros Direct), which the filings tie to its disaggregated chip architectures [0000050863-26-000011:0022]. The members concern Intel only, and the filings name no direct relationships among them [0000050863-26-000011:0022].
findings: New Mexico is described as Intel's key advanced packaging facility, and a new advanced packaging facility is being built in Malaysia [0000050863-26-000011:0022].
Intel is expanding its New Mexico and Malaysia facilities, though it recently reduced the extent of the Malaysia expansion plans [0000050863-25-000009:0014].
EMIB entered high-volume manufacturing in 2017, and EMIB-T was introduced in 2025 with adoption expected to scale beginning in 2026 [0000050863-26-000011:0022].

Foveros, first introduced in 2019, has expanded to Foveros-B and Foveros-R, both targeted for high-volume manufacturing in 2027 [0000050863-26-000011:0022]. Foveros Direct, announced in 2025, is planned for hybrid-bonding support on Intel 18A-PT in 2028 [0000050863-26-000011:0022].
Intel's Ohio and Germany wafer facilities have been slowed or placed on hold, and its planned Poland assembly and test facility has also been put on hold [0000050863-25-000009:0014].

In 2024, Intel gave Apollo a stake in the rights to operate Fab 34 in Leixlip, Ireland, in exchange for a one-time capital infusion [0000050863-25-000009:0015]. Intel recognized a $755 million charge in Q4 2024 for expected penalties tied to construction delays under the Ireland SCIP arrangement [0000050863-26-000011:0068].

The Arizona campus expansion was supported by a 2022 joint investment with Brookfield, and as of the end of 2024 a significant majority of Intel's products were made on Intel 7 in Arizona and Israel [0000050863-25-000009:0015] [0000050863-25-000009:0014].

title: Intel processors, Gaudi 3 accelerators and open AI software
summary: The passages concern Intel only; AMD and NVIDIA appear only as competitors [0000050863-25-000009:0024]. The processor products are tied to Intel's manufacturing nodes, such as Intel 7, Intel 4, Intel 3 and Intel 18A [0000050863-26-000011:0021].
findings: Intel launched the Gaudi 3 AI accelerators in 2024, positioned with significant price-performance advantages for AI inference applications [0000050863-25-000009:0012].
OpenVINO is an open source toolkit that accelerates deep learning inference on Intel processors, and the filing calls it the leading inferencing library on Intel silicon [0000050863-25-000009:0012].

oneAPI lets developers write cross-architecture applications from a single code base across CPUs, GPUs and other accelerators, and Intel contributed its oneAPI specifications and implementations to the UXL Foundation under the Linux Foundation [0000050863-25-000009:0012].

Intel launched the Open Platform for Enterprise AI under the Linux Foundation in 2024 to speed deployment of generative AI use cases through modular microservice architecture [0000050863-25-000009:0012].

The Intel Xeon 6 processors launched in 2024 include P-cores with built-in matrix engines designed for compute-intensive workloads such as AI, alongside E-cores for scale-out, parallel workloads [0000050863-25-000009:0024].
Intel Xeon 6 Scalable server processor offerings are manufactured on the Intel 3 node [0000050863-26-000011:0021].
The Intel Core Ultra Series 1 was Intel's first AI PC processor, introduced in 2023 and manufactured on Intel 4 [0000050863-26-000011:0014] [0000050863-25-000009:0011].

The 13th and 14th Gen Intel Core processors, made on Intel 7, represented almost half of Intel's CCG product sales in 2025, and that share is expected to decrease significantly in 2026 as Intel Core Ultra sales rise [0000050863-26-000011:0014].

title: Market risk sensitivity: currency, interest rate, equity and commodity exposures
summary: This community is the market risk disclosure covering currency exchange rates, interest rates, equity prices and commodity prices, which recurs across two filings comparing December 2024 and December 2025 positions [0000050863-26-000011:0052]. The passages do not name the filing company; they are identified only by accession prefix 0000050863, so they cannot be tied to NVIDIA, AMD or Intel from the text alone [0000050863-25-000009:0079]. Most of the quantitative content concerns interest-rate exposure on debt and fixed-rate investments, and equity holdings in marketable and non-marketable securities [0000050863-26-000011:0053].
findings: A hypothetical 1% rise in interest rates would increase annual interest expense by approximately $97 million on debt outstanding at December 27, 2025, compared with $120 million for December 28, 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0052].

A weighted average adverse 10% change in currency exchange rates would reduce income before taxes by less than $38 million at December 27, 2025, versus less than $54 million at December 28, 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0052].
The fair value of marketable equity holdings fell from $0.8 billion at December 28, 2024 to $484 million at December 27, 2025 [0000050863-25-000009:0080] [0000050863-26-000011:0053].

The assumed equity price decline used for sensitivity moved from 55% to 45%, with the resulting potential decrease estimated at $218 million for 2025 against $466 million for 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0053].
The carrying amount of non-marketable equity investments rose from $4.5 billion at December 28, 2024 to $8.0 billion at December 27, 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0053].

Commodity price risk is described as not directly affecting the company to a material degree, though it operates facilities that consume commodities and uses hedging programs and sourcing plans to manage supplier concentration [0000050863-25-000009:0080] [0000050863-26-000011:0053].

The concentration of marketable equity holdings shifted from securities traded on the Shanghai Stock Exchange Science and Technology Innovation Board in 2024 to securities traded on the New York and Hong Kong stock exchanges in 2025 [0000050863-25-000009:0080] [0000050863-26-000011:0053].

title: Market risk disclosures: foreign exchange, interest rate and equity price exposure
summary: The disclosures cover a fiscal 10-K and a later 10-Q, and the foreign exchange and investment risk sections are shared across the reports. [0001045810-25-000023:0074] [0001045810-26-000021:0073] [0001045810-25-000230:0048]
findings: The company considers its direct foreign exchange exposure minimal because substantially all of its sales are in United States dollars, and foreign currency forward contracts are used to offset currency movements [0001045810-25-000023:0074].

A 10% strengthening of the U.S. dollar would have changed the amount recorded in accumulated other comprehensive income on foreign exchange contracts, before tax, by an adverse $180 million and $136 million as of January 25, 2026 and January 26, 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0073].

An adverse 10% foreign exchange change applied to balance sheet hedging contracts would have reduced income before taxes by $124 million and $129 million as of January 25, 2026 and January 26, 2025, respectively [0001045810-26-000021:0074].

The company carries $8.5 billion of senior Notes at a fixed rate, so it has no financial statement risk from changes in interest rates, although its fixed-rate investment portfolio is exposed to yield curve shifts [0001045810-26-000021:0073].
A parallel yield curve shift of plus or minus 0.5% would change the fair value of the investment portfolio by $238 million as of the end of fiscal year 2025 [0001045810-25-000023:0074].

Publicly-held equity securities are subject to market price volatility: a hypothetical 10% decrease would reduce their fair value by $1.8 billion as of January 25, 2026, and by $387 million as of October 26, 2025 in the 10-Q [0001045810-26-000021:0073] [0001045810-25-000230:0048].

Non-marketable equity securities are measured at cost minus impairment, adjusted for observable price changes, and their valuation is complex because market data is scarce [0001045810-26-000021:0073].
As of October 26, 2025, the 10-Q reports no material changes to the foreign exchange rate risks described in the prior annual report [0001045810-25-000230:0048].

title: Market risk disclosures: interest rate, default, FX and investment risk
summary: This community is the Item 7A market risk section of two annual filings by the same registrant, covering interest rate risk, default risk, foreign exchange risk and long-term investment risk [0000002488-25-000012:0079] [0000002488-26-000018:0083]. Interest rate and default risk are discussed together with the company's investment portfolio, and the outstanding long-term debt is described as fixed rate [0000002488-26-000018:0083]. Foreign exchange risk is tied to foreign operations and managed with derivative forward contracts [0000002488-26-000018:0084].
findings: A hypothetical 50 basis-point increase or decrease in interest rates would have changed the fair value of the cash equivalent and investment portfolio by about $6 million as of December 28, 2024, and by about $25 million as of December 27, 2025 [0000002488-25-000012:0079] [0000002488-26-000018:0083].

All outstanding long-term debt had fixed interest rates as of December 27, 2025, so exposure to rate changes on reported interest expense and cash flows is described as minimal [0000002488-26-000018:0083].

The company mitigates default risk by investing only in high credit quality securities, and all of its debt securities were A-rated by at least one rating agency as of December 28, 2024 and December 27, 2025 [0000002488-25-000012:0079] [0000002488-26-000018:0083].

Carrying value of investments in publicly traded companies was $198 million at December 27, 2025 versus $0 at December 31, 2024, and non-marketable equity securities and other instruments were $1.3 billion versus $468 million [0000002488-26-000018:0083].

Non-marketable investments in privately held companies are often in a start-up or early development stage, are inherently risky, and may result in a loss of the investment [0000002488-26-000018:0083].
The aggregate notional amount of foreign currency forward contracts was $3.4 billion as of December 27, 2025, up from $2.8 billion a year earlier [0000002488-26-000018:0084].

The estimated net fair-value position of those forwards moved from a $66 million loss at December 28, 2024 to a $12 million gain at December 27, 2025, and the contracts cover currencies including the Indian Rupee, Canadian Dollar and Chinese Renminbi [0000002488-26-000018:0084].

title: Intel government equity, Altera and NAND divestitures, SCIP partnerships and segments
summary: These reports are mainly about Intel: the U.S. government's equity stake tied to CHIPS Act funding, the Altera and NAND divestitures, and the Silver Lake and SK hynix transactions [0000050863-25-000179:0068][0000050863-25-000074:0022]. Intel's SCIP partnerships with Brookfield, Apollo and Bain Capital bring outside capital into its fabs, while its CCG, DCAI and NEX segments make up Intel Products [0000050863-24-000124:0016][0000050863-26-000011:0010]. NVIDIA's filings contribute only the 2020 Share Purchase Agreement among NVIDIA, Arm, SoftBank and Vision Fund, which appears in its exhibit index [0001045810-25-000023:0131].
findings: The transactions eliminate contractual rights to receive future grant funds under the commercial CHIPS Act and may limit the company's ability to secure government grants in the future [0000050863-25-000179:0068].

The U.S. government was one of the company's largest stockholders at 5.8% as of September 27, 2025, and may acquire up to an additional 3.2% as Secure Enclave disbursements are received [0000050863-25-000179:0068].

The Altera sale is expected to yield about $4.4 billion in net cash proceeds, and $1.0 billion of the purchase price is deferred into two $500 million installments due by December 31, 2026 and December 31, 2027 [0000050863-25-000074:0022].

Apollo's 2024 transaction involved the sale of 49% of Intel's interest in Ireland SCIP for net proceeds of $11.0 billion, and Ireland SCIP has the rights to operate Fab 34 in Leixlip, Ireland [0000050863-24-000124:0016].
Intel recognized a $755 million charge in the fourth quarter of 2024 for penalties it expects to pay in connection with Ireland SCIP construction delays [0000050863-26-000011:0068].

In fiscal 2024, CCG generated $30,290 million of revenue and $10,920 million of operating income, versus $12,817 million of revenue for DCAI and $5,842 million of revenue for NEX [0000050863-25-000009:0111].
CCG's primary competitor is AMD, which like Intel designs processors based on the x86 architecture [0000050863-26-000011:0010].

Intel's Section 13(r) disclosure covers dealings with the Federal Security Service of the Russian Federation and Positive Technologies, and the FSB dealings are explicitly authorized by General License 1B [0000050863-25-000179:0071].

title: AMD risks: Intel and Nvidia competition, supply chain and customer dependence
summary: This community collects AMD risk factors on competing with Intel and Nvidia, dependence on Microsoft and other software vendors, and reliance on a small set of customers [0000002488-25-000012:0022][0000002488-26-000018:0036][0000002488-25-000012:0028]. Its supply chain and distribution risks cover third-party logistics, gray market sales, product defects and distributor credit [0000002488-25-000012:0039][0000002488-25-000012:0040][0000002488-25-000012:0041][0000002488-25-000012:0038]. Other passages in the group address environmental rules, debt covenants and goodwill impairment, and they name AMD rather than NVIDIA or Intel [0000002488-26-000018:0050][0000002488-26-000018:0053][0000002488-26-000018:0057].
findings: Intel's aggressive pricing and special incentives have in the past resulted in lower unit sales and a lower average selling price for many of AMD's products [0000002488-25-000012:0022].
AMD expects intense competition from Nvidia in the supply of GPUs and other accelerators for the AI market [0000002488-25-000012:0023].

AMD expects a small number of customers to continue to account for a substantial part of its revenue, which increases the risk of customers defaulting on or delaying payments [0000002488-25-000012:0028].
AMD's semi-custom SoC revenue depends on those products being incorporated into customers' products and on the success of those products [0000002488-25-000012:0020].

AMD's microprocessors are not designed to work with motherboards built for Intel microprocessors, and its ability to innovate beyond the x86 instruction set depends partly on Microsoft designing operating systems to run on its products [0000002488-26-000018:0036].

Nearly all product assembly and final testing is performed at third-party facilities in China, Malaysia and Taiwan, and geopolitical changes between China and Taiwan could disrupt Taiwan-based wafer foundries and subcontractors [0000002488-26-000018:0058].

AMD extends credit to some distributors and AIB partners and protects their inventory against price reductions, so a significant price decline would reduce AMD's revenue and gross margin [0000002488-25-000012:0038].
AMD says gray market products create shadow inventory that is not visible to it, making demand difficult to forecast [0000002488-25-000012:0041].

title: NVIDIA US export controls on China and data center products
summary: This community concerns NVIDIA's exposure to US export controls and licensing rules on its data center and China-bound GPUs, including the H20, H200, GB200, A100 and H100 lines [0001045810-25-000209:0034][0001045810-24-000124:0028]. Its linked items include the AI Diffusion rule, which the USG said in May 2025 it would rescind in favor of a replacement with uncertain scope [0001045810-25-000209:0035], and the April 2025 license requirement for H20 exports to China [0001045810-25-000230:0035]. The passages come only from NVIDIA's filings, and none of them cover AMD or Intel [0001045810-25-000116:0046].
findings: In April 2025 the USG required a license for H20 exports to China, and NVIDIA recorded a $4.5 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal 2026 for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations [0001045810-25-000230:0035].

An earlier filing said no H20 products had shipped under the August 2025 China licenses, while a later filing reports approximately $50 million of H20 revenue under those licenses [0001045810-25-000209:0054][0001045810-25-000230:0035].
The AI Diffusion IFR would have imposed a worldwide licensing requirement on NVIDIA's most recent data center products, such as the H200, GB200 and GB300 [0001045810-25-000209:0034].

NVIDIA says it has not received licenses to ship restricted products to China, and the Notified Advanced Computing process has not resulted in approvals for China customers [0001045810-24-000264:0056][0001045810-24-000124:0050].

NVIDIA states that its competitive position has been harmed by export controls and could be further harmed if licenses are delayed or denied or if customers buy from competitors [0001045810-25-000116:0049].
NVIDIA warns that government mandates for chip tracking and throttling could introduce system vulnerabilities and expose it to significant risk and potential liability [0001045810-25-000116:0049].

Regulators in China have inquired about NVIDIA's sales and its fulfillment of Mellanox acquisition commitments, and are investigating whether compliance with US export controls discriminates against China customers [0001045810-25-000023:0040].
The French Competition Authority collected information from NVIDIA about its graphics card and cloud service provider business as part of an ongoing inquiry [0001045810-25-000209:0050].

title: NVIDIA platforms, demand and supply risk, export controls and derivative litigation
summary: This community concerns NVIDIA, covering its market platforms, software products and two reportable segments, Compute & Networking and Graphics [0001045810-24-000264:0027][0001045810-24-000264:0034]. Its risk side links inaccurate demand estimates, long manufacturing lead times and product transitions to inventory charges and supply mismatches [0001045810-25-000116:0041]. Export controls and China restrictions add further exposure, and a separate thread covers shareholder derivative suits tied to the securities litigation [0001045810-24-000316:0058][0001045810-24-000124:0021].
findings: Data Center revenue was up 154% from a year ago, driven by demand for the Hopper GPU computing platform for training and inferencing of large language models [0001045810-24-000264:0034].

For the second quarter of fiscal year 2026, sales to Customer A represented 23% of total revenue and sales to Customer B represented 16%, both attributable to the Compute & Networking segment [0001045810-25-000209:0039].

A $4.5 billion charge for H20 excess inventory and purchase obligations in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026 partially offset growth in Compute & Networking segment operating income for the first half [0001045810-25-000209:0039].

NVIDIA states that inaccurate demand estimates have resulted in both product shortages and excess inventory, and that this mismatch has significantly harmed its financial results [0001045810-24-000124:0041].
NVIDIA's gross margins in the second quarter of fiscal year 2025 were negatively impacted by inventory provisions for low-yielding Blackwell material [0001045810-25-000230:0054].

NVIDIA says it has not received licenses to ship its restricted Blackwell products to China, and the NAC licensing process has not resulted in approvals for exports to Chinese customers [0001045810-24-000316:0058].

The Chinese government announced an Action Plan endorsing compute performance per watt and per memory bandwidth standards for accelerators, which NVIDIA says could prevent it from designing compliant products if modified or implemented adversely [0001045810-24-000264:0059].

The Supreme Court dismissed NVIDIA's writ of certiorari as improvidently granted on December 11, 2024, and the Ninth Circuit's judgment took effect on February 20, 2025, remanding the case to the district court [0001045810-25-000209:0025].

title: AMD segments, MI308 export control and customer and international sales exposure
summary: This community concerns AMD alone, and the passages describe no NVIDIA or Intel entities [0000002488-26-000018:0012]. It covers AMD's product lines, including EPYC and Ryzen CPUs, Radeon and Instinct GPUs, Pensando DPUs and Virtex, Kintex, Artix, Spartan and Zynq FPGAs and adaptive SoCs [0000002488-26-000018:0012][0000002488-26-000018:0007]. Its financial risk ties Data Center and Client and Gaming results to the MI308 export control, customer concentration and international sales [0000002488-25-000166:0033][0000002488-24-000056:0034].
findings: Data Center net revenue rose 32% to $16.6 billion in 2025 from $12.6 billion in 2024, driven by demand for AMD EPYC processors and Instinct GPU accelerators [0000002488-26-000018:0077].

Approximately $440 million of net inventory and related charges tied to the U.S. government export control on AMD Instinct MI308 products weighed on Data Center operating income in 2025 [0000002488-26-000018:0077].

For the nine months ended September 27, 2025, about $800 million of MI308 export control charges contributed to Data Center operating income falling to $1.9 billion from $2.3 billion a year earlier [0000002488-25-000166:0033].
International sales were 67% of net revenue in 2025 and 66% in 2024, and AMD expects them to remain a significant portion of total sales [0000002488-26-000018:0077].
AMD says it depends on a small number of customers for a substantial portion of its business [0000002488-24-000056:0034].
AMD's semi-custom SoC products power the Sony PlayStation 5 and the Microsoft Xbox Series S and X game consoles [0000002488-26-000018:0009].

title: AMD's ZT Systems, Xilinx and Pensando deals, Sanmina sale, OpenAI agreement and related risks
summary: This community centers on AMD's acquisitions of ZT Systems, Xilinx, Pensando and Silo AI, the later sale of ZT Systems' manufacturing business to Sanmina, and AMD's OpenAI product agreement [0000002488-26-000018:0072][0000002488-25-000012:0101][0000002488-24-000163:0025]. The passages describe AMD's own filings, so the community concerns AMD rather than NVIDIA or Intel [0000002488-26-000018:0005]. The related risk factors cover acquisition integration, goodwill impairment, debt covenants, government approvals, supply chain and gray market diversion [0000002488-25-000012:0053][0000002488-25-000108:0080][0000002488-24-000163:0067][0000002488-24-000163:0056].
findings: AMD completed the acquisition of ZT Systems on March 31, 2025, paying $3.2 billion in cash and issuing 8,335,849 shares of common stock [0000002488-25-000166:0030].

AMD completed the sale of the ZT Manufacturing Business to Sanmina on October 27, 2025 for 1,151,052 Sanmina shares and $2.4 billion in cash, with up to $450 million more contingent on certain conditions [0000002488-25-000166:0030].

In October 2025 AMD entered a product purchase agreement with OpenAI OpCo, LLC to deploy 6 gigawatts of AMD GPUs, with the first gigawatt powered by AMD Instinct MI450 series products [0000002488-26-000018:0072]. AMD also issued OpenAI a warrant for up to 160 million shares at $0.01 per share [0000002488-25-000166:0030].

AMD completed the Xilinx acquisition on February 14, 2022 for a total purchase consideration of $48.8 billion, allocating $22.8 billion to goodwill [0000002488-25-000012:0101]. The Pensando acquisition, completed May 26, 2022, was valued at about $1.9 billion and allocated $1.1 billion to goodwill [0000002488-25-000012:0101].

New U.S. export restrictions on certain semiconductors to China led to about $800 million in MI308 inventory and related charges in the second quarter of fiscal 2025, and about $360 million of those charges was later reversed after AMD began shipping under U.S. licenses [0000002488-26-000018:0072].

If the ZT Systems acquisition is not completed, AMD would have to pay ZT Systems a $300 million termination fee in certain circumstances tied to failure to obtain required regulatory approvals [0000002488-24-000163:0070].

AMD has been named a responsible party at three Superfund sites in Sunnyvale, California, and has entered into settlement agreements with other responsible parties on two of the related cleanup orders [0000002488-24-000163:0063].

title: Third-party foundry, wafer and packaging dependence at AMD and Intel
summary: This community concerns how AMD and Intel depend on outside foundries, packaging partners and supply agreements, with TSMC, GF, UMC, Samsung and Tongfu named as key manufacturers [0000002488-25-000012:0030]. AMD's filings describe its reliance on TSMC and GF for wafers and on ATMP joint ventures with Tongfu affiliates for assembly and test [0000002488-24-000163:0046] [0000002488-24-000163:0047], while Intel's filings describe the risks of its own third-party foundry business [0000050863-26-000011:0061]. AMD's filings also describe yield and limited-supplier risks in its manufacturing chain [0000002488-24-000163:0049].
findings: AMD relies on TSMC for all of its wafers for microprocessor and GPU products at 7 nm or smaller nodes, and relies primarily on GLOBALFOUNDRIES for those products at larger nodes [0000002488-24-000163:0046].

AMD's earlier 2024 filing describes its wafer supply agreement with GF as running through 2025, while a later filing says it sets minimum annual capacity allocation and pricing through 2026 [0000002488-24-000056:0039] [0000002488-24-000163:0047].
Intel Foundry revenue fell to 17,543 million dollars in 2024 from 18,910 million in 2023, while its operating loss widened to 13,408 million from 6,955 million [0000050863-25-000009:0032].

Intel has no long-term contract with TSMC, and it says only TSMC and Samsung are currently capable of producing the leading-edge and near-leading-edge nodes its products need [0000050863-26-000011:0065].

Intel's disaggregated design uses tiles made by TSMC or other third-party foundries, so an interruption could delay complete products until replacement tiles are designed and sourced [0000050863-26-000011:0063].
Lower manufacturing yields could raise per-unit costs, hurt gross margin and force AMD to allocate reduced product supply among its customers [0000002488-25-000108:0055].
AMD's third-party manufacturers also fabricate for competitors and could prioritize other customers or raise prices on short notice [0000002488-25-000047:0041].

summary: The passages are NVIDIA's filing text, and the reports name no AMD filing text [0001045810-25-000023:0022]. title: Intel patent, EC fine and Spectre/Meltdown litigation
summary: These reports cover Intel's legal proceedings: the VLSI patent suits and Finjan license defense, the R2 Semiconductor patent suits and August 2024 settlements, the European Commission fine and Spectre/Meltdown litigation, and the EireOg and Media Content Protection suits against Intel customers [0000050863-25-000109:0037] [0000050863-24-000124:0035] [0000050863-24-000076:0027] [0000050863-26-000011:0177]. Intel is the defendant or the party bearing the exposure in each group, although the EireOg complaints also accuse AMD CPUs [0000050863-26-000011:0177]. Several matters carry accrued charges or indemnity obligations, including a roughly $1.0 billion VLSI accrual and $780 million in R2-related charges [0000050863-25-000009:0160] [0000050863-24-000149:0034].
findings: VLSI filed three infringement suits against Intel in April 2019 in the Western District of Texas, accusing various processors of infringing eight patents VLSI acquired from NXP [0000050863-25-000109:0037].

In the first Texas case the court entered a final judgment of $2.2 billion in damages plus about $162 million in interest in April 2022, and in December 2023 the Federal Circuit vacated the damages award tied to the $675 million verdict [0000050863-25-000109:0037].

As of December 28, 2024, Intel had accrued a charge of approximately $1.0 billion related to the VLSI litigation and said it could not reasonably estimate losses above that amount [0000050863-25-000009:0160].

The Dusseldorf Regional Court found in February 2024 that Intel's processors infringe R2's European patent and issued an injunction and recall order against Intel and its customers [0000050863-24-000124:0035].

Intel recorded a $780 million charge in the second quarter of 2024 for three confidential settlement agreements with R2, Third Point and TRGP Capital, and the later filing says Intel expects to pay that aggregate amount [0000050863-24-000149:0034] [0000050863-25-000009:0161].

The European Commission imposed a €1.1 billion fine in 2009 that Intel paid in 2009, the General Court annulled the rebates findings and that fine in January 2022, and the Court of Justice dismissed the EC's appeal in October 2024 [0000050863-24-000076:0027] [0000050863-24-000124:0031] [0000050863-24-000149:0035].

US consumer class actions over Spectre and Meltdown were consolidated in Oregon, where final judgment went to Intel in July 2022 and the Ninth Circuit affirmed in November 2023 [0000050863-24-000076:0028].

EireOg Innovations has filed eleven complaints since April 2024 in Texas federal courts against Intel and AMD customers, and Intel is indemnifying Acer, AWS, Cisco, Dell, HPE, HPI, IBM, Lenovo and Oracle over the claims [0000050863-26-000011:0177].

title: AMD risk factors on supply, distribution, export controls and Intel-NVIDIA competition
summary: This community is made up mainly of AMD risk factors from filing 0000002488-25-000166, covering supplier dependence, distribution and logistics, customer concentration, acquisitions and export controls [0000002488-25-000166:0043]. Several members link AMD to outside parties, including TSMC and GLOBALFOUNDRIES for wafers and the ATMP JVs for ATMP services [0000002488-25-000166:0050][0000002488-25-000166:0076]. One thread is the April 2025 U.S. license requirement on AMD Instinct MI308 exports to China, which led to about $800 million in charges [0000002488-25-000166:0057], and a smaller set adds Intel's announced NVIDIA partnership, which the filing treats as a competitive risk [0000002488-25-000166:0045][0000050863-26-000011:0007].
findings: AMD states that it relies on TSMC for all wafers for microprocessor and GPU products at 7 nm or smaller nodes, and primarily on GLOBALFOUNDRIES for those at larger nodes [0000002488-25-000166:0050].
AMD expects a small number of customers to continue to account for a substantial part of its revenue, so the loss of a key customer would materially affect its business [0000002488-25-000166:0049].

After an April 2025 U.S. license requirement restricted exports of its AMD Instinct MI308 products to China, AMD incurred approximately $800 million in inventory and related charges in the second quarter of 2025 [0000002488-25-000166:0057].

AMD's distributor and AIB partner agreements can generally be terminated for convenience on prior notice, are non-exclusive, and let those partners offer competitors' products [0000002488-25-000166:0059].
Gray market products result in shadow inventory that is not visible to AMD, making it difficult to forecast demand accurately [0000002488-25-000166:0062].

Some software drivers licensed for AMD's x86 products are certified by Microsoft, and AMD states that if Microsoft did not certify a driver or AMD otherwise lost Microsoft's support, its ability to market x86 products would be materially adversely affected [0000002488-25-000166:0059].

The filing says NVIDIA's September 2025 partnership and investment in Intel may increase competition and pricing pressure on its products [0000002488-25-000166:0045]. Intel states that it announced a strategic partnership with NVIDIA to co-develop custom client and data center products [0000050863-26-000011:0007].

title: AMD export controls, China joint ventures and related trade risk
summary: This community concerns AMD's export-control, tariff, China joint venture, climate and tax risk disclosures in its 10-K and 10-Q filings, centered on AMD Instinct and Versal products [0000002488-24-000123:0059][0000002488-25-000108:0065]. The export side covers the October 2023 BIS licensing requirements, the April 2025 MI308 license requirement, and the Entity List treatment of THATIC, a joint venture with Higon [0000002488-25-000012:0043][0000002488-25-000166:0063][0000002488-25-000012:0042]. The community also covers AMD's ATMP and THATIC joint ventures with Chinese partners, along with climate-related and tax risks [0000002488-24-000056:0012][0000002488-25-000012:0041][0000002488-26-000018:0046]. Every cited passage comes from an AMD filing, and the reports do not name NVIDIA or Intel [0000002488-25-000012:0042].
findings: Under the October 2023 BIS requirements, AMD cannot ship certain Instinct integrated circuits and certain Versal FPGAs to China, or to customers whose ultimate parent is in a D5 country, without a license [0000002488-25-000012:0043]. Certain Versal FPGAs also require a Notified Advanced Computing notification to BIS 25 days before shipment [0000002488-25-000047:0053].

AMD incurred approximately $800 million in inventory and related charges in the second quarter of 2025 because of the April 2025 license requirement covering its MI308 products [0000002488-25-000166:0063].

In August 2025 U.S. government officials expressed an expectation of receiving 15% of revenue from licensed MI308 sales to China, but no regulation had been published to establish that requirement [0000002488-25-000166:0064].

BIS announced in May 2025 its intention to rescind the January 2025 AI Diffusion Rule and issue replacement rules, which may require new export licenses or delay shipments [0000002488-25-000166:0064].

AMD's purchases from the ATMP JV were $1.7 billion in each of 2024 and 2023, and amounts payable to the ATMP JV rose from $363 million at December 30, 2023 to $476 million at December 28, 2024 [0000002488-25-000012:0104].
The carrying value of AMD's ATMP JV investment rose from $99 million at December 30, 2023 to $165 million at June 28, 2025 [0000002488-25-000108:0018].

AMD recognized licensing gains from royalty income under its February 2016 agreement with the THATIC JV of $48 million in 2024 and $34 million in 2023, while the carrying value of its THATIC JV investment was zero [0000002488-25-000012:0105].

title: Risk factors on debt, customers, litigation, cybersecurity and Mobileye
summary: This community groups risk-factor passages from 2024 and 2025 filings on debt and dividends, customer and distributor concentration, government contracts, litigation and IP claims, cybersecurity and data privacy, and the Mobileye goodwill charge [0000050863-25-000009:0072] [0000050863-26-000011:0081]. The group's reports say most passages do not name the filing company, though the cybersecurity report reads them as Intel's filings because they refer to Intel directors' cybersecurity experience [0000050863-26-000011:0092]. Many risks recur across the two years, with debt figures and credit facility sizes changing between them [0000050863-25-000009:0073] [0000050863-26-000011:0084].
findings: The three largest customers accounted for 45% of net revenue in 2024, 40% in 2023 and 42% in 2022, and the later filing reports 43% in 2025 [0000050863-25-000009:0071] [0000050863-26-000011:0083].

A significant portion of products is sold through distributors, value-added resellers, OEMs and ODMs, and a material change in a key distributor relationship could reduce revenue [0000050863-25-000009:0071].

Senior unsecured notes and other borrowings were $51.0 billion as of December 28, 2024 and $47.2 billion as of December 27, 2025 [0000050863-25-000009:0073] [0000050863-26-000011:0084]. The company suspended its quarterly dividend in the fourth quarter of 2024 and agreed under its CHIPS Act agreement to forgo dividends for two years [0000050863-25-000009:0073].

Non-practicing entities have brought costly suits, including the VLSI and R2 litigation, which produced significant adverse judgments and settlements [0000050863-26-000011:0080]. A February 2024 injunction and recall order obtained by R2 Semiconductor in a German court could have disrupted European business [0000050863-25-000009:0067].

The filings cite the 2020 SolarWinds compromise and the 2024 CrowdStrike outage as examples of supply-chain risk from widely adopted products, and Habana Labs had its network breached in the fourth quarter of 2020 [0000050863-25-000009:0065].

The later filing reports a $2.8 billion charge in the third quarter of 2024, primarily related to Mobileye goodwill [0000050863-26-000011:0082]. The earlier filing gives the charge as $2.9 billion [0000050863-25-000009:0070].

Government contracts are subject to procurement laws, and failure to comply can result in contract termination, fines, and suspension or debarment from future US government business [0000050863-25-000009:0072].
Regulation limiting perfluorocarbons and PFAS, which are critical to semiconductor manufacturing, could require abatement equipment and alter production processes [0000050863-25-000009:0076].

title: AMD Sunnyvale Superfund sites and AI, privacy and environmental compliance risk
summary: This community covers environmental, conflict minerals, labor, privacy and AI-related regulatory and risk-factor language, with the reports tying much of the environmental material to AMD [0000002488-25-000012:0017]. Its most specific thread is AMD's environmental exposure at three Superfund sites in Sunnyvale, California, for which AMD says it was named a responsible party [0000002488-25-000012:0018]. The AI, privacy and cybersecurity language comes from filings that do not name the company, including two filings with different filer IDs [0001045810-25-000023:0048] [0000002488-24-000163:0051].
findings: AMD says it has been named a responsible party at three Superfund sites in Sunnyvale, California, and is subject to Final Site Clean-up Requirements Orders from the California Regional Water Quality Control Board [0000002488-24-000123:0063].

AMD's estimated environmental liability was reported as approximately $5.5 million in one filing and approximately $5.9 million in a later filing, with no potential insurance recoveries recorded [0000002488-25-000012:0018] [0000002488-26-000018:0019].
The filing says that non-compliance with the GDPR could bring penalties of up to 20 million euros or 4% of worldwide revenue, whichever is greater [0001045810-25-000023:0048].
Data broadly defined as important under China's law may not be transferable outside China without prior assessment and approval by the Cyberspace Administration of China [0001045810-26-000021:0050].

One filing describes the EU AI Act as something being considered, while a later filing says it was adopted in 2024 and will be phased in over the next few years [0000002488-24-000123:0065] [0000002488-25-000047:0061].

AMD incurs costs to comply with conflict minerals reporting, and customers requiring conflict-free components may choose a competitor's products if those demands are not met [0000002488-24-000123:0064].

title: Intel 14A foundry dependence, fabs, packaging and AI processor lines
summary: These reports concern Intel only, covering its leading-edge roadmap centered on Intel 14A and its dependence on a significant external foundry customer [0000050863-26-000011:0008]. They also cover Intel's manufacturing footprint, its advanced packaging technologies, and its processor and Gaudi 3 AI accelerator products [0000050863-26-000011:0022] [0000050863-25-000009:0012]. Intel links the 14A question to its facility plans, saying a pause would also affect planned manufacturing expansions [0000050863-26-000011:0034].
findings: Intel says that if it cannot secure a significant external foundry customer for Intel 14A, it may pause or discontinue Intel 14A and successor leading-edge process technologies [0000050863-26-000011:0008].

Intel says any decision to pause or discontinue Intel 14A and successor nodes may be effectively irreversible, given the years of R&D, intellectual property and facility investment involved [0000050863-25-000109:0065].

In 2025 Intel began consolidating its Costa Rican assembly and test operations into existing sites in Vietnam and Malaysia, slowed construction of the new Ohio fab, and discontinued planned expansions in Germany and Poland [0000050863-26-000011:0034].
Intel's Ohio and Germany wafer facilities have been slowed or placed on hold, and its planned Poland assembly and test facility has also been put on hold [0000050863-25-000009:0014].
Intel recognized a $755 million charge in Q4 2024 for expected penalties tied to construction delays under the Ireland SCIP arrangement [0000050863-26-000011:0068].
EMIB entered high-volume manufacturing in 2017, and EMIB-T was introduced in 2025 with adoption expected to scale beginning in 2026 [0000050863-26-000011:0022].
Intel launched the Gaudi 3 AI accelerators in 2024, positioned with significant price-performance advantages for AI inference applications [0000050863-25-000009:0012].

The 13th and 14th Gen Intel Core processors, made on Intel 7, represented almost half of Intel's CCG product sales in 2025, and that share is expected to decrease significantly in 2026 as Intel Core Ultra sales rise [0000050863-26-000011:0014].

title: Intel Arizona Fab, AMD debt indentures and exhibit agreements
summary: This community covers agreements of Intel, AMD and NVIDIA, most of them listed as exhibits in the companies' filings [0000050863-26-000011:0187] [0000002488-25-000012:0138]. Its Intel part centers on Arizona Fab LLC, a joint venture formed in 2022 through a transaction with Brookfield Asset Management, which Intel consolidates [0000050863-24-000076:0015]. Its AMD part covers senior notes and indentures, a Lantana HP sublease, a Nantong Fujitsu equity purchase agreement, executive offer letters and a Wells Fargo credit agreement [0000002488-25-000012:0106] [0000002488-26-000018:0144] [0000002488-25-000012:0141].
findings: Intel has an unrecognized commitment to fund its share of the total construction costs of Arizona Fab, which is $29.0 billion [0000050863-24-000076:0015]. Intel will be the sole operator of two new chip factories built by Arizona Fab and must operate Arizona Fab at minimum wafer-start production levels or face penalties [0000050863-24-000076:0015].

Non-controlling interest in Arizona Fab LLC was $2,760 million at March 30, 2024, reflecting 49% non-controlling ownership, and Arizona Fab's assets of $5.6 billion can be used only to settle its own obligations [0000050863-24-000076:0015].

AMD issued $1.0 billion of 3.924% and 4.393% senior notes on June 9, 2022, under an indenture with U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association as trustee [0000002488-25-000012:0106]. Holders can require repurchase at 101% of principal plus accrued interest if AMD undergoes a change of control [0000002488-25-000012:0106].

The Xilinx 2.2375% Senior Notes due 2030 are governed by a Second Supplemental Indenture dated February 14, 2022, among Xilinx, Inc., Advanced Micro Devices, Inc. and U.S. Bank Trust Company, National Association [0000002488-25-000012:0138].

AMD subleases space from Lantana HP, LTD under a Sublease Agreement dated March 26, 2013, paired with a Master Landlord's Consent to Sublease signed by 7171 Southwest Parkway Holdings, L.P., Lantana HP, Ltd. and AMD [0000002488-25-000012:0138].

AMD's Credit Agreement is dated April 29, 2022, names Wells Fargo Bank, National Association as administrative agent, and was filed as Exhibit 10.1 to AMD's Current Report on Form 8-K dated April 29, 2022 [0000002488-25-000012:0141] [0000002488-26-000018:0146].

NVIDIA's patent cross license with Intel, dated January 10, 2011, is listed as Intel exhibit 10.11, while AMD's patent cross license with Intel, dated November 11, 2009, is incorporated by reference in AMD's exhibit index [0000050863-25-000009:0170] [0000002488-25-000012:0138].

The exhibit numbers of the Jean Hu offer letter and sign-on bonus agreement shifted between AMD's filings, from 10.57 and 10.58 in the earlier index to 10.52 and 10.53 in the later one [0000002488-25-000012:0141] [0000002488-26-000018:0146].

title: Market risk sensitivity: currency, interest rate, equity and commodity exposures
summary: This community is a market risk disclosure covering currency exchange rates, interest rates, equity prices and commodity prices, compared across December 2024 and December 2025 positions [0000050863-26-000011:0052]. The passages identify the filer only by accession prefix 0000050863, so they do not tie the disclosure to NVIDIA, AMD or Intel from the text alone [0000050863-25-000009:0079]. Most of the quantitative content concerns interest-rate exposure on debt and equity holdings in marketable and non-marketable securities [0000050863-26-000011:0053].
findings: A hypothetical 1% rise in interest rates would increase annual interest expense by about $97 million on debt outstanding at December 27, 2025, versus $120 million at December 28, 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0052].

A weighted average adverse 10% change in currency exchange rates would reduce income before taxes by less than $38 million at December 27, 2025, compared with less than $54 million at December 28, 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0052].
The fair value of marketable equity holdings fell from $0.8 billion at December 28, 2024 to $484 million at December 27, 2025 [0000050863-25-000009:0080] [0000050863-26-000011:0053].

The assumed equity price decline used in the sensitivity analysis moved from 55% to 45%, with the estimated potential decrease at $218 million for 2025 against $466 million for 2024 [0000050863-26-000011:0053].
The carrying amount of non-marketable equity investments rose from $4.5 billion at December 28, 2024 to $8.0 billion at December 27, 2025 [0000050863-26-000011:0053].

Commodity price risk is described as not directly affecting the company to a material degree, though it operates facilities that consume commodities and uses hedging programs and sourcing plans to manage supplier concentration [0000050863-25-000009:0080] [0000050863-26-000011:0053].

The concentration of marketable equity holdings shifted from securities traded on the Shanghai Stock Exchange Science and Technology Innovation Board in 2024 to securities traded on the New York and Hong Kong stock exchanges in 2025 [0000050863-25-000009:0080] [0000050863-26-000011:0053].

title: Market risk disclosures: foreign exchange, interest rate and equity price exposure
summary: This community covers market risk disclosures from a fiscal 10-K and a later 10-Q, and the foreign exchange and investment risk sections are shared across these reports [0001045810-25-000023:0074] [0001045810-26-000021:0073] [0001045810-25-000230:0048]. It centers on foreign exchange sensitivity, the fixed-rate investment portfolio's exposure to yield curve shifts, and the price volatility of publicly-held equity securities [0001045810-26-000021:0073].
findings: Direct foreign exchange exposure is described as minimal because substantially all sales are in United States dollars, and foreign currency forward contracts are used to offset currency movements [0001045810-25-000023:0074].

A 10% strengthening of the U.S. dollar would have changed the amount recorded in accumulated other comprehensive income on foreign exchange contracts, before tax, by an adverse $180 million and $136 million as of January 25, 2026 and January 26, 2025 [0001045810-26-000021:0073].

An adverse 10% foreign exchange change applied to balance sheet hedging contracts would have reduced income before taxes by $124 million and $129 million as of January 25, 2026 and January 26, 2025, respectively [0001045810-26-000021:0074].

The company carries $8.5 billion of senior Notes at a fixed rate, so it reports no financial statement risk from changes in interest rates, although its fixed-rate investment portfolio is exposed to yield curve shifts [0001045810-26-000021:0073].
A parallel yield curve shift of plus or minus 0.5% would change the fair value of the investment portfolio by $238 million as of the end of fiscal year 2025 [0001045810-25-000023:0074].

A hypothetical 10% decrease would reduce the fair value of publicly-held equity securities by $1.8 billion as of January 25, 2026, and by $387 million as of October 26, 2025 in the 10-Q [0001045810-26-000021:0073] [0001045810-25-000230:0048].

Non-marketable equity securities are measured at cost minus impairment, adjusted for observable price changes, and their valuation is complex because market data is scarce [0001045810-26-000021:0073].
As of October 26, 2025, the 10-Q reports no material changes to the foreign exchange rate risks described in the prior annual report [0001045810-25-000230:0048].
